title.zh: 卷三十 列傳第二十 何尚之
title.raw: 卷三十 列傳第二十 何尚之 Volume 30 Biographies 20: He Shangzhi

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十

translations.literal: Biographies 20
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 20

sentences.zh: 何尚之

translations.literal: He Shangzhi
translations.idiomatic: He Shangzhi

sentences.zh: 尚之少頗輕薄，好摴蒱，及長，折節蹈道，以操立見稱。

translations.literal: In youth Shangzhi was rather frivolous and fond of dice games; when he grew older he restrained himself and followed the Way, gaining repute for his conduct and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi was frivolous in youth and addicted to dice, but as he matured he reformed and held to the Way, earning renown for uprightness.

sentences.zh: 為陳郡謝混所知，與之遊處。

translations.literal: He came to be known by Xie Hun of Chen Commandery and associated with him in friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hun of Chen Commandery took notice of him, and they became companions.

sentences.zh: 家貧，初為臨津令。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he first served as Magistrate of Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: Born poor, he first served as magistrate of Linjin.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝領征西將軍，補主簿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song held the post of General Who Conquers the West, Shangzhi was appointed as his Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu served as General Who Conquers the West, Shangzhi joined his staff as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 從征長安，以公事免，還都。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Chang'an, was dismissed for an official offense, and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Chang'an, was dismissed for an official offense, and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 因患勞病積年，飲婦人乳乃得差。

translations.literal: He then suffered from chronic consumptive illness for years and recovered only after drinking a woman's milk.
translations.idiomatic: Chronic consumptive illness plagued him for years until he recovered by drinking a woman's milk.

sentences.zh: 以從征之勞，賜爵都鄉侯。

translations.literal: For his service on the campaign he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: For campaign service he received the title Marquis of Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，為廬陵王義真車騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shao acceded, Shangzhi became Consultation Officer on the staff of Prince of Luling Yizhen's Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shao took the throne, Shangzhi served as consultation officer on Prince of Luling Yizhen's chariots-and-cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 義真與司徒徐羨之、尚書令傅亮等不協，每有不平之言。

translations.literal: Yizhen was at odds with Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi, Secretariat Director Fu Liang, and others, and often spoke words of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen clashed with Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and other senior ministers and often voiced his grievances.

sentences.zh: 尚之諫戒不納。

translations.literal: Shangzhi admonished and warned him, but Yizhen would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi warned him repeatedly, but Yizhen paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 義真被廢，入為中書侍郎，遷吏部郎。

translations.literal: When Yizhen was deposed, Shangzhi entered the capital as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat and was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizhen's deposition, Shangzhi entered court as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat and was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 告休定省，傾朝送別於冶渚。

translations.literal: When he requested leave to visit his parents, the whole court turned out to see him off at Yezhu.
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave to visit his parents, the whole court turned out to see him off at Yezhu.

sentences.zh: 及至郡，叔度謂曰：「聞汝來此，傾朝相送，可有幾客？

translations.literal: When he reached his commandery, his uncle said to him: "I hear that since you came here the whole court has turned out to send you off—how many guests were there?"
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post his uncle asked, "I hear the whole court saw you off—how many guests were there?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「殆數百人。

translations.literal: "He replied, "Nearly several hundred people."
translations.idiomatic: "Nearly several hundred," he replied.

sentences.zh: 」叔度笑曰：「此是送吏部郎耳，非關何彥德也。

translations.literal: His uncle laughed and said, "This was seeing off the Director in the Ministry of Personnel—it had nothing to do with He Yande."
translations.idiomatic: His uncle laughed. "They were seeing off the personnel director, not He Yande."

sentences.zh: 昔殷浩亦嘗作豫章定省，送別者甚眾，及廢徙東陽，船泊征虜亭積日，乃至親舊無復相窺者。」

translations.literal: "In former times Yin Hao also once went to Yuzhang on a family visit, and those who saw him off were very numerous; yet when he was deposed and exiled to Dongyang, his boat moored at Zheng Lu Pavilion for days, and even close kin and old friends no longer came to visit."
translations.idiomatic: "Yin Hao once drew huge farewell crowds when he visited Yuzhang on family leave, yet after his deposition and exile to Dongyang his boat lay at Zheng Lu Pavilion for days without a single close friend calling."

sentences.zh: 後拜左衛將軍，領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General of the Left Guard and concurrently Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made General of the Left Guard and concurrently Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 尚之雅好文義，從容賞會，甚為文帝所知。

translations.literal: Shangzhi by nature loved literary elegance; in leisurely gatherings he was greatly appreciated by Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi loved literary elegance, and in leisurely gatherings Emperor Wen came to know him well.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十三年，彭城王義康欲以司徒長史劉斌為丹陽尹，上不許，乃以尚之為之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanjia, Prince of Pengcheng Yikang wished to appoint Senior Administrator Liu Bin as Governor of Danyang, but the Emperor did not permit it and instead made Shangzhi governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 13, Prince of Pengcheng Yikang wanted Liu Bin as Governor of Danyang; the Emperor refused and appointed Shangzhi instead.

sentences.zh: 立宅南郭外，立學聚生徒。

translations.literal: He built a residence outside the southern wall and established a school to gather students.
translations.idiomatic: He built a house outside the southern wall and opened a school to gather students.

sentences.zh: 東海徐秀，廬江何曇、黃回，潁川荀子華，太原孫宗昌、王延秀，魯郡孔惠宣並慕道來遊，謂之南學。

translations.literal: Xu Xiu of Donghai, He Tan and Huang Hui of Lujiang, Xun Zihua of Yingchuan, Sun Zongchang and Wang Yanxiu of Taiyuan, and Kong Huixuan of Lu Commandery all admired the Way and came to study with him—the school was called the Southern Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiu of Donghai, He Tan and Huang Hui of Lujiang, Xun Zihua of Yingchuan, Sun Zongchang and Wang Yanxiu of Taiyuan, and Kong Huixuan of Lu all came to study with him—the Southern Academy.

sentences.zh: 王球常云：「尚之西河之風不墜。

translations.literal: Wang Qiu often said, "Shangzhi has not let the wind of the Western River fall."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiu said, "Shangzhi keeps the Western River tradition alive."

sentences.zh: 」尚之亦云：「球正始之風尚在。」

translations.literal: Shangzhi also said, "Qiu still preserves the Zhengshi wind."
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi replied, "Qiu still carries the Zhengshi spirit."

sentences.zh: 尚之女適劉湛子黯，而湛與尚之意好不篤。

translations.literal: Shangzhi's daughter was married to Liu Zhan's son An, yet Liu Zhan and Shangzhi were not on close terms.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi's daughter married Liu Zhan's son An, yet the two men were not close.

sentences.zh: 湛欲領丹陽，乃徙尚之為祠部尚書，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan wished to take charge of Danyang himself and therefore transferred Shangzhi to Director of the Ministry of Rites, concurrently Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan wanted Danyang for himself and moved Shangzhi to Director of the Ministry of Rites, concurrently Director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 尚之甚不平。

translations.literal: Shangzhi was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi nursed deep resentment.

sentences.zh: 湛誅，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: After Liu Zhan was executed, Shangzhi was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Zhan's execution, Shangzhi became Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時左衛將軍范曄任參機密，尚之察其意趣異常，白文帝：「宜出為廣州，若在內釁成，不得不加以鈇鉞。

translations.literal: At that time General of the Left Guard Fan Ye held a role in state secrets; Shangzhi perceived that his intent and conduct were abnormal and reported to Emperor Wen: "He should be sent out to Guangzhou; if rebellion arises within the palace, the axe and halberd cannot be withheld."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye then held a role in state secrets; Shangzhi saw something abnormal in him and told Emperor Wen, "Send him to Guangzhou—if rebellion brews inside the palace, you cannot withhold the axe."

sentences.zh: 屢誅大臣，有虧皇化。

translations.literal: "Repeated executions of great ministers have harmed the imperial transformation."
translations.idiomatic: "Each execution of a great minister has chipped away at the throne's moral authority."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「始誅劉湛等，方欲引升後進。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Having just executed Liu Zhan and the others, I now wish to promote the younger generation."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "We have just executed Liu Zhan and his circle; now I wish to promote younger men."

sentences.zh: 曄事蹟未彰，便豫相黜斥，萬姓將謂卿等不能容才，以我為信受讒說。

translations.literal: "Fan Ye's deeds are not yet manifest; to dismiss him in advance—the people will say you cannot tolerate talent and that I believe slander."
translations.idiomatic: "Fan Ye's guilt is not yet clear; to dismiss him now would make the people say you cannot tolerate talent and that I believe slander."

sentences.zh: 但使共知如此，不憂致大變也。

translations.literal: "But let them all know this, and I need not fear a great upheaval."
translations.idiomatic: "Let them all know this, and I need not fear a great upheaval."

sentences.zh: 」曄後謀反伏誅，上嘉其先見。

translations.literal: Later Fan Ye plotted rebellion and was executed; the Emperor praised Shangzhi's foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye later rebelled and was executed; the Emperor praised Shangzhi's foresight.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he became Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he became Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是歲造玄武湖，上欲于湖中立方丈、蓬萊、瀛洲三神山，尚之固諫乃止。

translations.literal: That year the Black Tortoise Lake was constructed; the Emperor wished to erect the three sacred mountains Fangzhang, Penglai, and Yingzhou within the lake, but Shangzhi firmly remonstrated and the plan was halted.
translations.idiomatic: That year Black Tortoise Lake was dug; the Emperor wanted three sacred isles within it, but Shangzhi's remonstrance stopped the plan.

sentences.zh: 時又造華林園，並盛暑役人。

translations.literal: At the same time the Hualin Garden was also being built, and laborers were conscripted in the height of summer.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Hualin Garden was built, conscripting labor in midsummer.

sentences.zh: 尚之又諫，上不許，曰：「小人常日曝背，此不足為勞。

translations.literal: Shangzhi remonstrated again; the Emperor would not agree and said, "Common folk sun their backs every day—this is no hardship."
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi remonstrated again; the Emperor refused, saying, "Common folk sun their backs every day—this is no hardship."

sentences.zh: 」時上行幸，還多侵夜，尚之又表諫，上優詔納之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor went on tour and often returned deep into the night, Shangzhi again submitted a memorial of remonstrance; the Emperor responded with a gracious edict and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial tours kept the Emperor out until deep night, Shangzhi remonstrated again; the Emperor answered graciously and accepted.

sentences.zh: 先是患貨少，鑄四銖錢，人間頗盜鑄，多翦鑿古錢以取銅，上患之。

translations.literal: Previously there had been a shortage of coin; four-zhu cash was cast, but illicit casting was widespread and people clipped and chiseled ancient coins for copper—the Emperor was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Coin was scarce; four-zhu cash was cast, but illicit casting spread and people clipped ancient coins for copper—the Emperor was troubled.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，錄尚書江夏王義恭議，以一大錢當兩，以防翦鑿，議者多同。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, at the recorded deliberation of the Secretariat, Prince of Jiangxia Yigong proposed that one large coin equal two, to prevent clipping and chiseling; most in the deliberation agreed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 Prince of Jiangxia Yigong proposed one large coin equal two to stop clipping; most agreed.

sentences.zh: 尚之議曰：「凡創制改法，宜順人情，未有違眾矯物而可久也。

translations.literal: Shangzhi argued: "Whenever institutions are newly created or laws changed, one should follow human sentiment; never has defying the multitude and forcing things endured long."
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi argued: "New institutions must follow human sentiment; nothing that defies the multitude endures."

sentences.zh: 泉布廢興，未容驟議。

translations.literal: "The rise and fall of currency cannot be debated in haste."
translations.idiomatic: "Currency cannot be debated in haste."

sentences.zh: 前代赤仄白金，俄而罷息，六貨憒亂，人泣於市。

translations.literal: "In former ages the Red Foot and white metal were quickly abolished; the Six Goods brought chaos, and people wept in the markets."
translations.idiomatic: "Former ages saw Red Foot and white metal quickly abolished, the Six Goods bring chaos, and people weep in markets."

sentences.zh: 良由事不畫一，難用遵行。

translations.literal: "Truly because matters lacked unity, they were hard to implement."
translations.idiomatic: "Matters lacked unity and could not be implemented."

sentences.zh: 自非急病權時，宜守長世之業。

translations.literal: "Unless there is urgent crisis and temporary need, one should preserve the long-lasting enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: "Unless crisis demands it, preserve the long-lasting enterprise."

sentences.zh: 若今制遂行，富人之貲自倍，貧者彌增其困，懼非所以欲均之意。

translations.literal: "If the present measure is carried out, the rich will double their wealth and the poor will be further pressed—I fear this is not the intent of seeking equality."
translations.idiomatic: "If this measure proceeds, the rich double their wealth and the poor suffer more—not the intent of equality."

sentences.zh: 」中領軍沈演之以為若以大錢當兩，則國傳難朽之寶，家贏一倍之利，不俟加憲，巧源自絕。

translations.literal: Central Army Commander Shen Yanzhi held that if one large coin equaled two, the state would possess imperishable treasure and households would gain double profit; without adding penalties, clever schemes would die of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yanzhi held that one large coin equal to two would give the state imperishable treasure and households double profit, ending fraud without new penalties.

sentences.zh: 上從演之議，遂以一錢當兩。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed Yanzhi's proposal and made one coin equal two.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor followed Yanzhi and made one coin equal two.

sentences.zh: 行之經時，公私非便，乃罷。

translations.literal: After it had been in effect for some time, public and private affairs were both inconvenienced, and the measure was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After a time public and private affairs were both inconvenienced, and the measure was abolished.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，為尚書令、太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十九年致仕，于方山著退居賦以明所守，而議者咸謂尚之不能固志。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he retired from office and wrote the "Rhapsody on Retirement at Mount Fang" at Fangshan to declare his principles, yet critics all said Shangzhi could not hold firm to his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he retired and wrote the "Rhapsody on Retirement at Mount Fang" to declare his principles, yet critics said he could not hold firm.

sentences.zh: 文帝與江夏王義恭詔曰：「羊、孟尚不得告謝，尚之任遇有殊，便當未宜申許。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen issued an edict to Prince of Jiangxia Yigong: "Yang and Meng were not granted leave to resign; Shangzhi's appointments and favor are exceptional—approval should not yet be granted."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen told Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, "Yang and Meng were not granted leave to resign; Shangzhi's favor is exceptional—do not yet approve."

sentences.zh: 」尚之還攝職。

translations.literal: Shangzhi returned to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi returned to his duties.

sentences.zh: 羊即羊玄保，孟即孟顗。

translations.literal: "Yang" was Yang Xuanbao and "Meng" was Meng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: "Yang" meant Yang Xuanbao; "Meng" meant Meng Yi.

sentences.zh: 尚之既任事，上待之愈隆，於是袁淑乃錄古來隱士有跡無名者，為真隱傳以嗤焉。

translations.literal: Once Shangzhi resumed office, the Emperor treated him with even greater favor; thereupon Yuan Shu compiled a "Biography of True Recluses" of ancient hermits who left traces but no names, to mock him.
translations.idiomatic: Once back in office the Emperor favored him more; Yuan Shu compiled a "Biography of True Recluses" to mock him.

sentences.zh: 時或遣軍北侵，資給戎旅，悉以委之。

translations.literal: When armies were sometimes sent north on raids, supplies for the troops were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When armies raided north, supplies for the troops were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 元凶弑立，進位司空、尚書令。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince assassinated the Emperor and usurped the throne, Shangzhi was promoted to Minister of Works and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the Crown Prince murdered the Emperor and seized the throne, Shangzhi was elevated to Minister of Works and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時三方興義，將佐家在都者，劭悉欲誅之。

translations.literal: At that time the three regions had risen in righteous cause; among the staff whose families were in the capital, the usurper wished to execute them all.
translations.idiomatic: Three regions had risen in righteous cause; the usurper wished to execute staff whose families were in the capital.

sentences.zh: 尚之誘說百端，並得全免。

translations.literal: Shangzhi persuaded him with every argument and all were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi argued every way he could, and all were spared.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，復為尚書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu acceded, Shangzhi again became Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Shangzhi again headed the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丞相南郡王義宣、車騎將軍臧質反，義宣司馬竺超、質長史陸展兄弟並應從誅，尚之上言於法為重，超從坐者由是得原。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Prince of Nanjun Yixuan and General of Chariots and Cavalry Zang Zhi rebelled, Yixuan's staff officer Zhu Chao and Zhi's senior administrator Lu Zhan and his brothers all deserved execution by association; Shangzhi submitted that under the law the penalty was severe, and those associated with Chao were thereby pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Nanjun Yixuan and Zang Zhi rebelled, Zhu Chao and Lu Zhan's brothers deserved execution by association; Shangzhi argued the penalty was too severe, and Chao's associates were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 時欲分荊州置郢州，議其所居。

translations.literal: At that time it was proposed to split Jing Province and establish Ying Province; they deliberated where its seat should be.
translations.idiomatic: It was proposed to split Jing Province and establish Ying Province; they deliberated its seat.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭、蕭思話以為宜在巴陵。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and Xiao Sihua held that it should be at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and Xiao Sihua held it should be at Baling.

sentences.zh: 尚之議曰：「夏口在荊、江之中，正對沔口，通接雍、梁，寔為津要，於事為允。

translations.literal: Shangzhi argued: "Xiakou lies between Jing and the Yangtze, directly facing Hankou and connecting with Yong and Liang—it is truly a strategic crossing and suitable in every respect."
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi argued: "Xiakou lies between Jing and the Yangtze, facing Hankou and connecting Yong and Liang—a true strategic crossing."

sentences.zh: 」上從其議。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 荊、揚二州戶口居江南之半，江左以來，揚州為根本，委荊州以閫外，至是並分，欲以削臣下之權。

translations.literal: The registered households of Jing and Yang provinces comprised half the population south of the Yangtze; since the Eastern Jin, Yangzhou had been the root and Jingzhou entrusted with outer defense—now both were split to reduce the power of subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Yang held half the south's population; since Eastern Jin Yang had been root and Jing outer defense—now both were split to reduce subordinates' power.

sentences.zh: 而荊、揚並因此虛耗。

translations.literal: Yet Jing and Yang both suffered depletion because of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both Jing and Yang were drained by the split.

sentences.zh: 尚之建言宜復合二州，上不許。

translations.literal: Shangzhi proposed that the two provinces should be reunited; the Emperor would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi proposed reuniting the two provinces; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，以為左光祿、開府儀同三司，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming he was made Left Grand Master of the Palace, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and continued as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 2 he was made Left Grand Master of the Palace with golden seal and purple ribbon, continuing as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 尚之在家，常著鹿皮帽。

translations.literal: At home Shangzhi often wore a deerskin cap.
translations.idiomatic: At home he habitually wore a deerskin cap.

sentences.zh: 及拜開府，天子臨軒，百僚陪位，沈慶之於殿庭戲之曰：「今日何不著鹿皮冠？

translations.literal: When he was appointed Grand Master with Golden Seal, the Son of Heaven came to the hall and the hundred officials attended; Shen Qingzhi jested in the courtyard: "Why not wear your deerskin cap today?"
translations.idiomatic: At his grand-master appointment the Son of Heaven came to court; Shen Qingzhi jested in the courtyard, "Why not wear your deerskin cap today?"

sentences.zh: 」慶之累辭爵命，朝廷敦勸甚苦。

translations.literal: Qingzhi repeatedly declined enfeoffment, and the court pressed him with great insistence.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi repeatedly declined enfeoffment, and the court pressed him hard.

sentences.zh: 尚之謂曰：「主上虛懷側席，詎宜固辭。

translations.literal: Shangzhi said to him, "The sovereign holds an open mind and waits with folded mat—how can you stubbornly refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi said, "The sovereign waits with folded mat—how can you stubbornly refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」慶之曰：「沈公不效何公去而復還也。

translations.literal: Qingzhi said, "Shen does not imitate Master He, who left and then returned."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "Shen will not copy Master He—leave office, then crawl back."

sentences.zh: 」尚之有愧色。

translations.literal: Shangzhi flushed with shame.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi colored with shame.

sentences.zh: 尚之愛尚文義，老而不休。

translations.literal: Shangzhi loved and honored literary elegance and never ceased even in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi loved literary elegance and never ceased even in old age.

sentences.zh: 與太常顏延之少相好狎，二人並短小，尚之常謂延之為沐，延之目尚之為猴。

translations.literal: He and Grand Master of Ceremonies Yan Yanzhi had been close since youth; both were short in stature—Shangzhi often called Yanzhi "Bather" and Yanzhi called Shangzhi "Monkey."
translations.idiomatic: He and Yan Yanzhi had been close since youth; both were short—Shangzhi called Yanzhi "Bather" and Yanzhi called Shangzhi "Monkey."

sentences.zh: 同游太子西池，延之問路人云：「吾二人誰似猴？

translations.literal: Once they strolled at the Crown Prince's Western Pool; Yanzhi asked a passerby, "Which of us two looks more like a monkey?"
translations.idiomatic: At the Crown Prince's Western Pool Yanzhi asked a passerby, "Which of us looks more like a monkey?"

sentences.zh: 」路人指尚之為似。

translations.literal: The passerby pointed to Shangzhi as the likeness.
translations.idiomatic: The passerby pointed to Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 延之喜笑，路人曰：「彼似猴耳，君乃真猴。」

translations.literal: Yanzhi laughed with delight; the passerby said, "He merely resembles a monkey—you are the real monkey."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi laughed; the passerby said, "He merely resembles a monkey—you are the real monkey."

sentences.zh: 有人嘗求為吏部郎，尚之歎曰：「此敗風俗也。

translations.literal: Someone once sought appointment as Director in the Ministry of Personnel; Shangzhi sighed and said, "This will ruin custom."
translations.idiomatic: Someone once sought appointment as personnel director; Shangzhi sighed, "This will ruin custom."

sentences.zh: 官當圖人，人安得圖官。

translations.literal: "Office should seek men—how can men seek office?"
translations.idiomatic: "Office should choose men—men must not choose office."

sentences.zh: 」延之大笑曰：「我聞古者官人以才，今官人以勢，彼勢之所求，子何疑焉。

translations.literal: Yanzhi laughed loudly and said, "I hear that in antiquity men were appointed for talent; now men are appointed for power. What he seeks by power—why do you doubt it?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi laughed, "In antiquity men were appointed for talent; now for power. What he seeks by power—why doubt it?"

sentences.zh: 」所與延之論議往反，並傳於世。

translations.literal: The debates and exchanges between Shangzhi and Yanzhi were all transmitted in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Debates between Shangzhi and Yanzhi circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 尚之立身簡約，車服率素，妻亡不娶，又無姬妾。

translations.literal: Shangzhi conducted himself with simple restraint; his carriage and dress were plain, and after his wife died he took no wife and kept no concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi lived simply; carriage and dress were plain, and after his wife died he took no wife and kept no concubines.

sentences.zh: 執衡當朝，畏遠權柄，親故一無薦舉。

translations.literal: Holding the scales of office, he feared and kept distant from power; among kin and friends he recommended no one.
translations.idiomatic: Holding office he kept distant from power; among kin and friends he recommended no one.

sentences.zh: 既以此致怨，亦以此見稱。

translations.literal: He incurred resentment for this, yet was also praised for it.
translations.idiomatic: He incurred resentment for this, yet was also praised.

sentences.zh: 復以本官領中書令。

translations.literal: He again held his original post and concurrently served as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He resumed his former post and also directed the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 薨年七十九，贈司空，諡曰簡穆公。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-nine; posthumously he was made Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Duke of Jianmu.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-nine; posthumously he was made Minister of Works with the title Duke of Jianmu.

sentences.zh: 子偃。

translations.literal: His son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan.

sentences.zh: 偃字仲弘，元嘉中，位太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Yan, styled Zhonghong, during Yuanjia served as Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Zhonghong, served in Yuanjia as Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 元凶弑立，以偃為侍中，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince assassinated the Emperor and usurped the throne, Yan was made Palace Attendant in charge of edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince usurped the throne, Yan became Palace Attendant in charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 時尚之為司空、尚書令，偃居門下。

translations.literal: At that time Shangzhi was Minister of Works and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Yan served at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi was Minister of Works and Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Yan served at the gate.

sentences.zh: 父子並處權要，時為寒心；

translations.literal: Father and son both held positions of power at once, and the age trembled for them;
translations.idiomatic: Father and son both held power at once, and the age trembled;

sentences.zh: 而尚之及偃善攝機宜，曲得時譽。

translations.literal: yet Shangzhi and Yan were skilled at handling the moment and subtly won contemporary praise.
translations.idiomatic: yet Shangzhi and Yan handled the moment skillfully and won contemporary praise.

sentences.zh: 會孝武即位，任遇無改。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu acceded, their appointments and favor were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu acceded, their appointments were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 歷位侍中，領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He successively served as Palace Attendant and Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Palace Attendant and Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 時求讜言，偃以為「宜重農恤本，並官省事，考課以知能否，增奉以除吏奸。

translations.literal: When candid counsel was sought, Yan proposed: "Agriculture and the root should be heavily emphasized, offices consolidated and affairs reduced, examinations instituted to know ability, and salaries increased to remove official corruption.
translations.idiomatic: When candid counsel was sought, Yan proposed: "Emphasize agriculture, consolidate offices, examine ability, and raise salaries to curb corruption.

sentences.zh: 責成良守，久於其職；

translations.literal: Good governors should be charged with long tenure in their posts;
translations.idiomatic: Good governors should hold long tenure;

sentences.zh: 都督刺史，宜別其任」。

translations.literal: regional inspectors and governors should have their duties separated."
translations.idiomatic: regional inspectors and governors should have separate duties."

sentences.zh: 改領驍騎將軍，親遇隆密，有加舊臣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Valiant Cavalry; imperial favor was close and dense, exceeding that shown old ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Valiant Cavalry; imperial favor exceeded that shown old ministers.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尚之去選未五載，偃復襲其跡，世以為榮。

translations.literal: Shangzhi had left the selection post less than five years before; Yan again followed in his footsteps—the age considered it glorious.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi had left personnel less than five years before; Yan followed in his footsteps—the age considered it glorious.

sentences.zh: 侍中顏竣至是始貴，與偃俱在門下，以文義賞會，相得甚歡。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yan Jun had only now risen to prominence and, with Yan, was at the gate; they delighted in literary gatherings and got on extremely well.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun had only now risen; he and Yan delighted in literary gatherings and got on extremely well.

sentences.zh: 竣既任遇隆密，謂宜居重大，而位次與偃等未殊，意稍不悅。

translations.literal: Once Jun's appointments and favor were close and dense, he felt he should hold weightier office, yet his rank was not yet distinguished from Yan's, and he grew somewhat displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jun's favor grew dense, he felt he deserved weightier office, yet his rank matched Yan's, and he grew displeased.

sentences.zh: 及偃代竣領選，竣逾憤懣，與偃遂隙。

translations.literal: When Yan replaced Jun in charge of selection, Jun grew ever more resentful and a rift opened between them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan replaced Jun in charge of selection, Jun grew resentful and a rift opened.

sentences.zh: 竣時權傾朝野，偃不自安，遂發悸病，意慮乖僻。

translations.literal: Jun then wielded power that tilted court and countryside; Yan could not feel secure and developed palpitations, his thoughts turning perverse.
translations.idiomatic: Jun wielded power across court and countryside; Yan grew insecure, developed palpitations, and his thoughts turned perverse.

sentences.zh: 上表解職，告靈不仕。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting release from office and reported his illness, refusing to serve.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial requesting release and reported illness, refusing to serve.

sentences.zh: 孝武遇偃既深，備加醫療乃得差。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, who favored Yan deeply, provided every medical treatment until he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu favored Yan deeply and provided every treatment until he recovered.

sentences.zh: 偃素好談玄，注莊子逍遙篇傳于時。

translations.literal: Yan had always loved discussing the abstruse and annotated the "Free and Easy Wandering" chapter of Zhuangzi, which circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Yan loved discussing the abstruse and annotated Zhuangzi's "Free and Easy Wandering," which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 卒官，孝武與顏竣詔，甚傷惜之。

translations.literal: He died in office; Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict with Yan Jun, deeply grieving his loss.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict with Yan Jun, deeply grieving.

sentences.zh: 諡曰靖。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Jing.

sentences.zh: 子戢。

translations.literal: His son Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji.

sentences.zh: 戢字慧景，選尚宋孝武長女山陰公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Huijing, was chosen to marry Emperor Xiaowu of Song's eldest daughter, Princess of Shanyin, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse for the Emperor's Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, styled Huijing, married Princess of Shanyin and was appointed Commandant of the Horse for the Emperor's Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 景和世，山陰主就帝求吏部郎褚彥回侍己，彥回雖拘逼，終不肯從。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era Princess of Shanyin asked the Emperor for Personnel Director Chu Yanhui to attend her; though pressed, Yanhui in the end would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinghe era Princess of Shanyin asked for Personnel Director Chu Yanhui; though pressed, Yanhui refused.

sentences.zh: 與戢同居止月餘日，由是特申情好。

translations.literal: He lived with Ji for more than a month, and from this their intimacy was specially deepened.
translations.idiomatic: He lived with Ji for more than a month, and their intimacy deepened.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，彥回參朝政，引戢為侍中，時年二十九。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui, Yanhui entered court governance and brought Ji in as Palace Attendant at the age of twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanhui's start Yanhui entered court governance and brought Ji in as Palace Attendant at twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 戢以年未三十，苦辭內侍，改授司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Ji, not yet thirty, strenuously declined inner service and was instead appointed Senior Administrator on the Minister of Works' left staff.
translations.idiomatic: Not yet thirty, Ji declined inner service and was appointed Senior Administrator on the Minister of Works' left staff.

sentences.zh: 戢美容儀，動止與褚彥回相慕，時人號為「小褚公」。

translations.literal: Ji had handsome features; in movement and bearing he emulated Chu Yanhui, and people of the time called him "Little Master Chu."
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in feature, Ji emulated Chu Yanhui in bearing—people called him "Little Master Chu."

sentences.zh: 家業富盛，性又華侈，衣被服飾，極為奢麗。

translations.literal: His family estate was rich and flourishing, and by nature he was extravagant; clothing, bedding, and adornments were extremely luxurious.
translations.idiomatic: His family was rich and he was extravagant; clothing and adornments were extremely luxurious.

sentences.zh: 出為吳興太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted Grand Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 上頗好畫扇，宋孝武賜戢蟬雀扇，善畫者顧景秀所畫。

translations.literal: The Emperor was rather fond of painted fans; Emperor Xiaowu of Song bestowed on Ji a cicada-and-sparrow fan painted by the skilled artist Gu Jingxiu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor loved painted fans; Emperor Xiaowu bestowed on Ji a cicada-and-sparrow fan by Gu Jingxiu.

sentences.zh: 時吳郡陸探微、顧寶先皆能畫，歎其巧絕。

translations.literal: At the time Lu Tanwei of Wu Commandery and Gu Baoxian could both paint; they sighed at its exquisite mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tanwei and Gu Baoxian could both paint; they sighed at its exquisite mastery.

sentences.zh: 戢因王晏獻之，上令晏厚酬其意。

translations.literal: Ji presented it through Wang Yan; the Emperor ordered Yan to reward him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Ji sent it via Wang Yan; the Emperor told Yan to reward him handsomely.

sentences.zh: 卒年三十六，諡懿子。

translations.literal: He died at thirty-six; his posthumous title was Duke of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-six and received the posthumous title Duke of Yi.

sentences.zh: 女為郁林王后。

translations.literal: His daughter became consort to Emperor of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter became consort to the Emperor of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 又追贈侍中、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant and Right Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Palace Attendant and Right Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 求字子有，偃弟子也。

translations.literal: Qiu, styled Ziyou, was Yan's younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu, styled Ziyou, was Yan's nephew.

sentences.zh: 父鑠，仕宋位宜都太守。

translations.literal: His father Shuo served Song as Grand Administrator of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuo served the Song as Grand Administrator of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 求元嘉末為文帝挽郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia Qiu served as a mourning officer for Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanjia's end Qiu served as a mourning officer for Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 歷位太子洗馬，丹陽郡丞，清退無嗜欲。

translations.literal: He successively served as Groom of the Heir Apparent, Assistant in Danyang Commandery, pure and retiring with no cravings.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Groom of the Heir Apparent and assistant in Danyang—pure, retiring, without cravings.

sentences.zh: 後為太子中舍人。

translations.literal: Later he became Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，妻亡，還吳葬舊墓。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era his wife died; he returned to Wu to bury her in the old tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi his wife died; he returned to Wu to bury her in the old tomb.

sentences.zh: 除中書郎，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat but declined.

sentences.zh: 仍住吳，隱居波若寺，足不踰戶，人莫見其面。

translations.literal: He still lived in Wu, secluded at Boruo Temple, never crossing the threshold, and no one saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Wu, secluded at Boruo Temple, never crossing the threshold—no one saw his face.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝崩，出奔國哀，除永嘉太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Song died, he came out to observe national mourning and was appointed Grand Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, he came out for national mourning and was appointed Grand Administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 求時寄住南澗寺，不肯詣台，乞於野外拜受，見許。

translations.literal: Qiu was then lodging at Nanjian Temple and would not go to court; he begged to receive appointment in the open country and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Lodging at Nanjian Temple, he would not go to court; he begged to receive appointment in the open country and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 一夜忽乘小船逃歸吳，隱武丘山。

translations.literal: One night he suddenly took a small boat and fled back to Wu, hiding on Mount Wuqiu.
translations.idiomatic: One night he fled by small boat back to Wu and hid on Mount Wuqiu.

sentences.zh: 齊永明四年，拜太中大夫，不就，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming of Qi he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace but did not take up the post and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Yongming 4 he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace but declined and died.

sentences.zh: 初，求父鑠素有風疾，無故害求母王氏，坐法死，求兄弟以此無宦情。

translations.literal: Earlier Qiu's father Shuo had long suffered from wind disorder and without cause killed Qiu's mother Lady Wang; he was executed by law, and Qiu and his brothers for this had no desire for office.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's father Shuo, afflicted with wind disorder, killed Qiu's mother and was executed; Qiu and his brothers therefore had no desire for office.

sentences.zh: 求弟點。

translations.literal: Qiu's younger brother Dian.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's younger brother Dian.

sentences.zh: 點字子皙，年十一，居父母憂，幾至滅性。

translations.literal: Dian, styled Zixi, at eleven lived in mourning for his parents and nearly destroyed himself in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Dian, styled Zixi, at eleven mourned his parents and nearly destroyed himself in grief.

sentences.zh: 及長，感家禍，欲絕昏宦，尚之強為娶琅邪王氏。

translations.literal: When he grew up, moved by the family calamity, he wished to renounce marriage and office; Shangzhi forced him to marry a Lady Wang of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, moved by family calamity, he wished to renounce marriage and office; Shangzhi forced him to marry a Lady Wang of Langya.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，將親迎，點累涕泣，求執本志，遂得罷。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete and he was about to go fetch the bride, Dian wept repeatedly and begged Qiu to uphold his original resolve; the marriage was then cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: When rites were complete and he was to fetch the bride, Dian wept and begged Qiu to uphold his resolve; the marriage was cancelled.

sentences.zh: 點明目秀眉，容貌方雅，真素通美，不以門戶自矜。

translations.literal: Dian had bright eyes and fine brows, handsome and dignified features, genuine simplicity and universal grace, and did not pride himself on his family standing.
translations.idiomatic: Bright-eyed with fine brows, handsome and dignified, genuinely simple, he did not pride himself on family standing.

sentences.zh: 博通群書，善談論。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in many books, he was skilled in discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly versed in books, he was skilled in discourse.

sentences.zh: 家本素族，親姻多貴仕。

translations.literal: The family was originally of plain lineage, yet kin by marriage mostly held noble office.
translations.idiomatic: The family was of plain lineage, yet kin by marriage mostly held noble office.

sentences.zh: 點雖不入城府，性率到，好狎人物。

translations.literal: Though Dian did not enter the prefectural city, by nature he was direct and fond of mixing with people.
translations.idiomatic: Though he did not enter the prefectural city, he was direct and fond of mixing with people.

sentences.zh: 遨遊人間，不簪不帶，以人地並高，無所與屈，大言踑踞公卿，敬下。

translations.literal: Roaming among people, uncombed and unbelted, by person and place both elevated he had no one to yield to; he spoke boldly and sat with legs sprawled before lords and ministers, yet was respectful to those below.
translations.idiomatic: Roaming uncombed and unbelted, elevated in person and place, he spoke boldly before lords yet was respectful below.

sentences.zh: 或乘柴車，躡草屩，恣心所適，致醉而歸。

translations.literal: Sometimes he rode a firewood cart or wore straw sandals, going wherever his heart led, and returned drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he rode a firewood cart or wore straw sandals, going wherever his heart led, returning drunk.

sentences.zh: 故世論以點為孝隱士，弟胤為小隱士，大夫多慕從之。

translations.literal: Therefore contemporary opinion called Dian a filial recluse and Yin a lesser recluse; many grandees admired and followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion called Dian a filial recluse and Yin a lesser recluse; many grandees admired and followed them.

sentences.zh: 時人稱重其通，號曰：「遊俠處士」。

translations.literal: People of the time praised his breadth and called him the "Wandering Knight Recluse."
translations.idiomatic: People praised his breadth and called him the "Wandering Knight Recluse."

sentences.zh: 兄求亦隱吳郡武丘山。

translations.literal: Elder brother Qiu also secluded himself on Mount Wuqiu in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Qiu also secluded himself on Mount Wuqiu.

sentences.zh: 求卒，點菜食不飲酒，訖於三年，腰帶減半。

translations.literal: When Qiu died, Dian ate vegetables and drank no wine until the three years were complete; his waistband was halved.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiu died, Dian ate vegetables and drank no wine for three years; his waistband was halved.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始末，徵為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: At the end of Taishi of Song he was summoned as Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At Song Taishi's end he was summoned as Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 齊初，累征中書侍郎、太子中庶子，並不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi he was repeatedly summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat and Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household, but never accepted.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi's start he was repeatedly summoned but never accepted.

sentences.zh: 與陳郡謝伷、吳國張融、會稽孔德璋為莫逆友。

translations.literal: With Xie You of Chen Commandery, Zhang Rong of Wu, and Kong Dezang of Kuaiji he was a sworn friend.
translations.idiomatic: With Xie You, Zhang Rong, and Kong Dezang he was a sworn friend.

sentences.zh: 點門世信佛，從弟遁以東籬門園居之，德璋為築室焉。

translations.literal: Dian's family for generations believed in Buddhism; his cousin Dun lived in the Eastern Hedge Gate garden, and Dezang built a dwelling for him.
translations.idiomatic: Dian's family believed in Buddhism for generations; cousin Dun lived in the Eastern Hedge Gate garden, and Dezang built his dwelling.

sentences.zh: 園有卞忠貞塚，點植花於塚側，每飲必舉酒酹之。

translations.literal: In the garden was the tomb of Bian Zhongzhen; Dian planted flowers beside the tomb and whenever he drank always raised a cup to libate it.
translations.idiomatic: Beside Bian Zhongzhen's tomb in the garden Dian planted flowers and always libated when he drank.

sentences.zh: 招攜勝侶，乃名德桑門，清言賦詠，優遊自得。

translations.literal: Inviting companions to fine outings, he named virtuous monks and engaged in pure talk, poetry, and leisurely roaming.
translations.idiomatic: Inviting fine companions and virtuous monks, he engaged in pure talk, poetry, and leisurely roaming.

sentences.zh: 初，褚彥回、王儉為宰相，點謂人曰：「我作齊書已竟，贊雲'回既世族，儉亦國華，不賴舅氏，遑恤國家'。

translations.literal: Earlier Chu Yanhui and Wang Jian were chancellors; Dian told someone, "I have already finished my History of Qi; the encomium reads, 'Hui was a clan of the age, Jian also a flower of the state—without relying on maternal kin, how could they care for the realm?'"
translations.idiomatic: When Chu Yanhui and Wang Jian were chancellors, Dian said, "I have finished my History of Qi: 'Hui was a clan of the age, Jian a flower of the state—without maternal kin, how could they care for the realm?'"

sentences.zh: 」王儉聞之，欲候點，知不可見，乃止。

translations.literal: Wang Jian heard this and wished to visit Dian but, knowing he could not be seen, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian heard and wished to visit but, knowing he could not be seen, stopped.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷命駕造點，點從後門遁去。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Jun ordered his carriage to visit Dian; Dian fled out the back gate.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yuzhang Jun ordered his carriage to visit; Dian fled out the back gate.

sentences.zh: 司徒竟陵王子良聞之，曰：「豫章王尚望塵不及，吾當望岫息心。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Prince of Jingling Ziliang heard this and said, "If even the Prince of Yuzhang cannot catch the dust, I should gaze at the mountain and quiet my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jingling Ziliang said, "If even Prince of Yuzhang cannot catch the dust, I should gaze at the mountain and quiet my heart."

sentences.zh: 」後點在法輪寺，子良就見之，點角巾登席，子良欣悅無已，遺點嵇叔夜酒杯、徐景山酒槍。

translations.literal: Later when Dian was at Falun Temple, Ziliang came to see him; Dian wore a kerchief and mounted the mat—Ziliang was endlessly delighted and gave Dian Ji Kang's wine cup and Xu Jingshan's wine ladle.
translations.idiomatic: At Falun Temple Ziliang came to see him; Dian wore a kerchief and mounted the mat—Ziliang was delighted and gave him Ji Kang's wine cup and Xu Jingshan's ladle.

sentences.zh: 點少時嘗患渴利，積歲不愈。

translations.literal: In youth Dian once suffered from wasting thirst and was ill for years without recovery.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Dian suffered wasting thirst for years without recovery.

sentences.zh: 後在吳中石佛寺建講，於講所晝寢，夢一道人，形貌非常，授丸一掬，夢中服之，自此而差，時人以為淳德所感。

translations.literal: Later at Shifo Temple in Wu he established a lecture hall; during the lecture he napped by day and dreamed of a daoist of extraordinary appearance who gave him a handful of pills—he swallowed them in the dream and from then recovered; people of the time took it as reward for pure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At Shifo Temple in Wu he lectured, napped, and dreamed a daoist gave him pills—in the dream he swallowed them and recovered; people took it as reward for pure virtue.

sentences.zh: 性通侻好施，遠近致遺，一無所逆，隨復散焉。

translations.literal: By nature he was free and easy and fond of giving; gifts arrived from near and far and he refused none, yet immediately gave them all away again.
translations.idiomatic: Free and easy, fond of giving, he refused no gift from near or far yet immediately gave all away.

sentences.zh: 嘗行經朱雀門街，有自車後盜點衣者，見而不言，旁人禽盜與之，點乃以衣施盜。

translations.literal: Once passing Vermilion Bird Gate Street, someone stole clothing from behind his cart; Dian saw but said nothing, and when bystanders seized the thief and returned the clothes, Dian gave the clothes to the thief.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Vermilion Bird Gate Street, someone stole from behind his cart; he said nothing, and when bystanders returned the clothes he gave them to the thief.

sentences.zh: 盜不敢受，點令告有司，盜懼乃受之。

translations.literal: The thief dared not accept; Dian ordered that officials be told, and the thief in fear then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The thief dared not accept; Dian ordered officials told, and the thief in fear accepted.

sentences.zh: 點雅有人倫鑒，多所甄拔。

translations.literal: Dian by nature had insight into human character and raised up many men.
translations.idiomatic: Dian had insight into character and raised up many men.

sentences.zh: 知吳興丘遲于幼童，稱濟陽江淹於寒素，悉如其言。

translations.literal: He recognized Qiu Chi of Wuxing as a child and praised Jiang Yan of Jiyang in humble circumstances—both turned out as he said.
translations.idiomatic: He recognized Qiu Chi as a child and praised Jiang Yan in humble circumstances—both as he said.

sentences.zh: 哀樂過人。

translations.literal: His joy and grief exceeded other men.
translations.idiomatic: Joy and grief in him outran other men.

sentences.zh: 嘗行逢葬者，歎曰：「此哭者之懷，豈可思邪。

translations.literal: Once on the road he met a funeral procession and sighed, "The feeling in this weeping—how can one not think on it?"
translations.idiomatic: Once he met a funeral and sighed, "The feeling in this weeping—how can one not think on it?"

sentences.zh: 」於是悲慟不能禁。

translations.literal: Thereupon he grieved and could not restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: He grieved and could not restrain himself.

sentences.zh: 老又娶魯國孔嗣女，嗣亦隱者。

translations.literal: In old age he again married a daughter of Kong Si of Lu, who was also a recluse.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he married a daughter of Kong Si of Lu, also a recluse.

sentences.zh: 點雖昏，亦不與妻相見，築別室以處之，人莫諭其意。

translations.literal: Though married, Dian still did not meet his wife face to face and built a separate chamber for her; no one understood his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Though married, he still did not meet his wife and built a separate chamber; no one understood why.

sentences.zh: 吳國張融少時免官，而為詩有高言，點答詩曰：「昔聞東都日，不在簡書前。

translations.literal: Zhang Rong of Wu in youth was dismissed from office yet wrote poetry with lofty words; Dian answered in verse: "In former days I heard of the Eastern Capital—before the written summons arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rong, dismissed from office, wrote lofty poetry; Dian answered, "In former days I heard of the Eastern Capital—before the written summons arrived."

sentences.zh: 」雖戲而融久病之。

translations.literal: Though in jest, Rong took it as a long-term wound.
translations.idiomatic: Though meant in jest, Rong nursed the barb for years.

sentences.zh: 及點後昏，融始為詩贈點曰：「惜哉何居士，薄暮遘荒淫。

translations.literal: When Dian later married, Rong at last wrote a poem for him: "Pity, Master He, in twilight you meet wild excess."
translations.idiomatic: When Dian later married, Rong wrote, "Pity, Master He, in twilight you meet wild excess."

sentences.zh: 」點亦病之。

translations.literal: Dian also took it as a wound.
translations.idiomatic: Dian too felt the sting for years.

sentences.zh: 永元中，崔慧景圍城，人間無薪，點悉伐園樹以贍親黨。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era Cui Huijing besieged the city; among the people there was no firewood, and Dian cut down all the trees in his garden to support kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan Cui Huijing besieged the city; without firewood Dian cut down his garden trees for kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 慧景性好佛義，先慕交點，點不顧之。

translations.literal: Huijing by nature loved Buddhist doctrine and had long admired acquaintance with Dian; Dian paid him no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing loved Buddhist doctrine and long admired Dian; Dian paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 至是乃逼召點，點裂裙為褲，往赴其軍，終日談說，不及軍事。

translations.literal: Now he forcibly summoned Dian; Dian tore his skirt into trousers, went to his army, and talked all day without touching military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He forcibly summoned Dian; Dian tore his skirt into trousers, went to his army, and talked all day without touching military affairs.

sentences.zh: 其語默之跡如此。

translations.literal: Such were the traces of his speech and silence.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ran the pattern of his speech and silence.

sentences.zh: 慧景平後，東昏大怒，欲誅之。

translations.literal: After Huijing was suppressed, Emperor Donghun was greatly enraged and wished to execute Dian.
translations.idiomatic: After Huijing was suppressed, Emperor Donghun wished to execute Dian.

sentences.zh: 王瑩為之懼，求計于蕭暢。

translations.literal: Wang Ying was afraid for him and sought a plan from Xiao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying was afraid and sought a plan from Xiao Chang.

sentences.zh: 暢謂茹法珍曰：「點若不誘賊共講，未必可量，以此言之，乃應得封。

translations.literal: Chang told Ru Fazhen, "If Dian had not lured the bandits to discourse together, the outcome might not have been measured; on this ground he ought to receive enfeoffment."
translations.idiomatic: Chang told Ru Fazhen, "Had Dian not lured the bandits to discourse, the outcome might differ—on this ground he ought to receive enfeoffment."

sentences.zh: 」東昏乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Donghun then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Donghun relented.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝與點有舊，及踐阼，手詔論舊，賜以鹿皮巾等，並召之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang had old ties with Dian; when he ascended the throne he sent a personal edict discussing old times, bestowed a deerskin kerchief and the like, and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang had old ties; on ascending he sent a personal edict, bestowed a deerskin kerchief, and summoned him.

sentences.zh: 點以巾褐引入華林園，帝贈詩酒，恩禮如舊，仍下詔徵為侍中。

translations.literal: Dian was led in wearing kerchief and coarse cloth to Hualin Garden; the Emperor presented poetry and wine with favor as of old and again issued an edict summoning him as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Led in kerchief and coarse cloth to Hualin Garden, the Emperor presented poetry and wine and summoned him as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 捋帝須曰：「乃欲臣老子。

translations.literal: He stroked the Emperor's beard and said, "So you wish to make a minister of old Lao!"
translations.idiomatic: He tugged the Emperor's beard and said, "So you mean to make a minister of old Lao!"

sentences.zh: 」辭疾不起。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and would not take office.

sentences.zh: 復下詔詳加資給，並出在所，日費所須，太官別給。

translations.literal: Another edict detailed additional provisions and granted everything needed day by day wherever he was, separately supplied by the Imperial Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict detailed provisions and granted daily needs wherever he was, separately from the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 天監二年卒，詔給第一品材一具，喪事所須，內監經理。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he died; an edict granted first-rank timber for one coffin, and the inner directorate managed funeral needs.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 2 he died; an edict granted first-rank timber and the inner directorate managed funeral needs.

sentences.zh: 點弟胤。

translations.literal: Dian's younger brother Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Dian's younger brother Yin.

sentences.zh: 胤字子季，出繼叔父曠，故更字胤叔。

translations.literal: Yin, styled Ziji, was adopted to his uncle Kuang and therefore also styled Yinishu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, styled Ziji, was adopted to uncle Kuang and also styled Yinishu.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，居憂，毀若成人。

translations.literal: At eight he lived in mourning; his grief was like an adult's.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he mourned; his grief was like an adult's.

sentences.zh: 及長輕薄不羈，晚乃折節好學，師事沛國劉瓛，受易及禮記、毛詩。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was frivolous and unrestrained; only in later years did he restrain himself and love learning, taking Liu Huan of Pei as teacher for the Changes, Record of Rites, and Mao Odes.
translations.idiomatic: Frivolous in youth, he later restrained himself and studied the Changes, Record of Rites, and Mao Odes under Liu Huan.

sentences.zh: 又入鍾山定林寺聽內典，其業皆通。

translations.literal: He also entered Dinglin Temple on Zhong Mountain to hear inner scriptures, and mastered them all.
translations.idiomatic: He also heard inner scriptures at Dinglin Temple on Zhong Mountain and mastered them all.

sentences.zh: 而縱情誕節，時人未之知也，唯瓛與汝南周顒深器異之。

translations.literal: Yet he indulged wild conduct, and people of the time did not yet know him—only Huan and Zhou Yong of Runan deeply valued and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he indulged wild conduct, unknown to his time—only Huan and Zhou Yong deeply valued him.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為建安太守，政有恩信，人不忍欺。

translations.literal: Serving Qi he was Grand Administrator of Jian'an; his governance had kindness and trust, and people could not bear to deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Administrator of Jian'an his governance had kindness and trust; people could not bear to deceive him.

sentences.zh: 每伏臘放囚還家，依期而反。

translations.literal: Each winter solstice and end-of-year he released prisoners to return home, and they came back on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Each winter solstice and year-end he released prisoners home, and they returned on schedule.

sentences.zh: 曆黃門侍郎，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He held Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王儉受詔撰新禮，未就而卒。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Jian received an edict to compile new rites but died before finishing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian received an edict to compile new rites but died before finishing.

sentences.zh: 又使特進張緒續成，緒又卒，屬在司徒竟陵王子良。

translations.literal: Special Advance Zhang Xu was ordered to continue and complete it; Xu also died, and the task fell to Minister of Works Prince of Jingling Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xu was ordered to continue; Xu also died, and the task fell to Prince of Jingling Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 子良以讓胤，乃置學士二十人佐胤撰錄。

translations.literal: Ziliang yielded to Yin and set twenty scholars to assist Yin in compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang yielded to Yin and set twenty scholars to assist him.

sentences.zh: 後以國子祭酒與太子中庶子王瑩並為侍中。

translations.literal: Later as Director of the Imperial University he and Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household Wang Ying both became Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Later as Director of the Imperial University he and Wang Ying both became Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 時胤單作祭酒，疑所服。

translations.literal: At that time Yin alone served as Director of the Imperial University and was uncertain what robe to wear.
translations.idiomatic: Yin alone served as Director of the Imperial University and was uncertain what robe to wear.

sentences.zh: 陸澄博古多該，亦不能據，遂以玄服臨試。

translations.literal: Lu Cheng was broadly learned in antiquity yet could not decide on authority; he therefore wore dark robes for the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng was broadly learned yet could not decide; he wore dark robes for the examination.

sentences.zh: 爾後詳議，乃用朱服。

translations.literal: After detailed deliberation, vermilion robes were used.
translations.idiomatic: After deliberation, vermilion robes were used.

sentences.zh: 祭酒朱服，自此始也。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial University in vermilion robes began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial University in vermilion robes began here.

sentences.zh: 及郁林嗣位，胤為後族，甚見親待。

translations.literal: When Emperor of Yulin succeeded, Yin as maternal kin was greatly favored and treated with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor of Yulin succeeded, Yin as maternal kin was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 為中書令，領臨海、巴陵王師。

translations.literal: He became Director of the Secretariat and concurrently tutor to the Princes of Linhai and Baling.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of the Secretariat and tutor to the Princes of Linhai and Baling.

sentences.zh: 胤雖貴顯，常懷止足。

translations.literal: Though Yin was noble and prominent, he always harbored the sense of knowing when to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Though noble and prominent, he always knew when to stop.

sentences.zh: 建武初，已築室郊外，恒與學徒游處其內。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he had already built a dwelling in the suburbs and constantly roamed and studied with disciples within it.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianwu's start he had built a suburban dwelling and roamed with disciples within it.

sentences.zh: 至是遂賣園宅欲入東。

translations.literal: Now he sold his garden and residence intending to go east.
translations.idiomatic: Now he sold garden and residence intending to go east.

sentences.zh: 未及發，聞謝朏罷吳興郡不還，胤恐後之，乃拜表解職，不待報輒去。

translations.literal: Before he could depart he heard Xie Tiao had left the post of Grand Administrator of Wuxing and would not return; Yin feared being left behind and submitted a memorial resigning without awaiting reply and left at once.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he heard Xie Tiao would not return from Wuxing; fearing to be left behind he resigned without awaiting reply.

sentences.zh: 明帝大怒，使御史中丞袁昂奏收胤。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming was greatly angered and had Imperial Censor Yuan Ang memorialize for Yin's arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming was enraged and had Yuan Ang memorialize for his arrest.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔許之。

translations.literal: Soon an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon approved his departure.

sentences.zh: 胤以會稽山多靈異，往游焉，居若邪山雲門寺。

translations.literal: Yin, because Kuaiji's mountains held many numinous marvels, went to wander there and lived at Yunmen Temple on Mount Ruoye.
translations.idiomatic: Because Kuaiji's mountains held numinous marvels, he wandered there and lived at Yunmen Temple on Mount Ruoye.

sentences.zh: 初，胤二兄求、點並棲遁，求先卒，至是胤又隱，世號點為「大山」，胤為「小山」，亦曰：「東山」。

translations.literal: Earlier Yin's two elder brothers Qiu and Dian both dwelt in seclusion; Qiu died first, and now Yin also hid—the age called Dian "Great Mountain" and Yin "Little Mountain," also saying "Eastern Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Qiu and Dian both dwelt in seclusion; Qiu died first, now Yin hid—Dian was "Great Mountain," Yin "Little Mountain," also "Eastern Mountain."

sentences.zh: 兄弟發跡雖異，克終皆隱，世謂何氏三高。

translations.literal: Though the brothers' beginnings differed, all ended in seclusion—the age called them the Three Heights of the He clan.
translations.idiomatic: Though beginnings differed, all ended in seclusion—the Three Heights of the He clan.

sentences.zh: 永元中，徵為太常、太子詹事，並不就。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era he was summoned as Grand Master of Ceremonies and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, but never accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan he was summoned as Grand Master of Ceremonies and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent but never accepted.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝霸朝建，引為軍謀祭酒，並與書詔，不至。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang established his hegemonic court, he was invited as Staff Officer for Military Planning and to draft edicts and letters, but did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang established its hegemonic court he was invited as staff officer and edict drafter but did not come.

sentences.zh: 及帝踐阼，詔為特進、光祿大夫，遣領軍司馬王杲之以手敕諭意，並征謝朏。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne, he was ordered Grand Master with Special Advance and Grand Master of the Palace; Army Commander Wang Gao was sent with a personal edict to explain the intent and summon Xie Tiao as well.
translations.idiomatic: On ascension he was ordered Grand Master with Special Advance; Wang Gao was sent with a personal edict to summon Xie Tiao as well.

sentences.zh: 杲之先至胤所，胤恐朏不出，先示以可起，乃單衣鹿皮巾執經卷，下床跪受。

translations.literal: Gao arrived at Yin's place first; Yin feared Tiao would not come out and first showed that rising was possible, then in single garment, deerskin kerchief, and holding a classic scroll descended the bed and knelt to receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Gao arrived first; Yin feared Tiao would not come, showed rising was possible, then in deerskin kerchief knelt to receive the edict.

sentences.zh: 詔出，就席伏讀。

translations.literal: When the edict was read he returned to his seat and read it prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was read he returned to his seat and read prostrate.

sentences.zh: 胤因謂杲之曰：「吾昔于齊朝欲陳三兩條事：一者欲正郊丘，二者欲更鑄九鼎，三者欲樹雙闕。

translations.literal: Yin then said to Gao, "In the Qi court I wished to present two or three matters: first to rectify the suburban and mound rites, second to recast the Nine Cauldrons, third to erect paired towers."
translations.idiomatic: Yin told Gao, "In Qi I wished to present three matters: rectify suburban rites, recast the Nine Cauldrons, erect paired towers."

sentences.zh: 世傳晉室欲立闕，王丞相指牛頭山雲，'此天闕也'。

translations.literal: "It is transmitted that the Jin house wished to erect towers; Chancellor Wang pointed at Oxhead Mountain's clouds and said, 'These are Heaven's towers.'"
translations.idiomatic: "Jin wished to erect towers; Chancellor Wang pointed at Oxhead Mountain's clouds and said, 'These are Heaven's towers.'"

sentences.zh: 是則未明立闕之意。

translations.literal: "Then the intent to erect towers was not yet clear."
translations.idiomatic: "That showed they had not grasped what a tower was for."

sentences.zh: 闕者謂之象魏，懸法於其上，浹日而收之。

translations.literal: "A tower means the Elephant and Glorious Hall—laws are suspended upon it, displayed at dawn and gathered at dusk."
translations.idiomatic: "A tower means the Elephant and Glorious Hall—laws suspended upon it, displayed at dawn and gathered at dusk."

sentences.zh: 象者法也，魏者當塗而高大貌也。

translations.literal: "Elephant means law; glorious means the appearance of blocking the road while standing high."
translations.idiomatic: "Elephant means law; glorious means blocking the road while standing high."

sentences.zh: 鼎者神器，有國所先。

translations.literal: "The cauldron is the divine vessel—the state's foremost possession."
translations.idiomatic: "The cauldron is the sacred vessel every state must possess first."

sentences.zh: 圓丘南郊，舊典不同。

translations.literal: "The round mound and southern suburb—old canons differ."
translations.idiomatic: "Round mound and southern suburb—old canons differ."

sentences.zh: 南郊祠五帝靈威仰之類，圓丘祠天皇大帝、北極大星是也。

translations.literal: "The southern suburb sacrifices to the Five Thearchs and Lingweiyang and the like; the round mound sacrifices to the Great Thearch of Heaven and the North Pole Star."
translations.idiomatic: "Southern suburb sacrifices to Five Thearchs; round mound to Great Thearch of Heaven and North Pole Star."

sentences.zh: 往代合之郊丘，先儒之巨失。

translations.literal: "Former generations combined suburban and mound rites—a great error of earlier scholars."
translations.idiomatic: "Earlier ages merged suburban and mound rites—the gravest error of the old scholars."

sentences.zh: 今梁德告始，不宜遂因前謬。

translations.literal: "Now Liang virtue announces its beginning—it is not fitting to follow the former error."
translations.idiomatic: "Now Liang virtue begins—it is not fitting to follow the former error."

sentences.zh: 卿宜陳之。

translations.literal: "You should present this."
translations.idiomatic: "You must raise these points at court."

sentences.zh: 」杲之曰：「僕之鄙劣，豈敢輕議國典，此當敬俟叔孫生耳。」

translations.literal: Gao said, "I am crude and inferior—how dare I lightly discuss state canons? This should await Master Shusun."
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, "I am crude—how dare I discuss state canons? This should await Master Shusun."

sentences.zh: 及杲之從謝朏所還，問胤以出期。

translations.literal: When Gao returned from Xie Tiao's place he asked Yin about the date of departure.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao returned from Tiao's place he asked Yin about departure.

sentences.zh: 胤知朏已應召，答杲之曰：「吾年已五十七，月食四斗米不盡，何容復有宦情？

translations.literal: Yin knew Tiao had already answered the summons and replied to Gao, "I am already fifty-seven; four dou of rice a month I cannot finish—how could I again harbor desire for office?"
translations.idiomatic: Yin knew Tiao had answered and replied, "I am fifty-seven; four dou of rice a month I cannot finish—how could I again desire office?"

sentences.zh: 」杲之失色不能答。

translations.literal: Gao turned pale and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Gao blanched and had no reply.

sentences.zh: 胤反謂曰：「卿何不遣傳詔還朝拜表，留與我同遊邪？

translations.literal: Yin in turn said, "Why not send the edict-bearer back to court to submit a memorial and stay to roam with me?"
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "Why not send the edict-bearer back to submit a memorial and stay to roam with me?"

sentences.zh: 」杲之愕然曰：「古今不聞此例。

translations.literal: Gao was startled and said, "From antiquity to the present no such precedent has been heard."
translations.idiomatic: Gao was startled: "From antiquity to the present no such precedent exists."

sentences.zh: 」胤曰：「檀弓兩卷，皆言物始。

translations.literal: Yin said, "The two volumes of T'an Kung both speak of things at the beginning."
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "T'an Kung's two volumes speak of things at the beginning."

sentences.zh: 自卿而始，何必有例？

translations.literal: "Begin with you—why must there be a precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: "Let the precedent start with you—why need there be an old one?"

sentences.zh: 」胤、朏俱前代高士，胤處名譽尤邁矣。

translations.literal: Yin and Tiao were both eminent men of the former age; Yin in reputation especially surpassed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Tiao were both eminent men of the former age; Yin especially surpassed in reputation.

sentences.zh: 杲之還，以胤意奏聞，有敕給白衣尚書祿。

translations.literal: When Gao returned he memorialized Yin's intent; an edict granted salary of Plain-robed Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gao memorialized Yin's intent; an edict granted salary of plain-robed Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 胤固辭。

translations.literal: Yin firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yin firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 又敕山陰庫錢月給五萬，又不受。

translations.literal: Another edict granted fifty thousand cash monthly from Shanyin treasury; again he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict granted fifty thousand cash monthly from Shanyin treasury; again he declined.

sentences.zh: 乃敕何子朗、孔壽等六人於東山受學。

translations.literal: Then an edict ordered He Zilang, Kong Shou, and six others to study on Eastern Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered He Zilang, Kong Shou, and six others to study on Eastern Mountain.

sentences.zh: 太守衡陽王元簡深加禮敬，月中常命駕式閭，談論終日。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Prince of Hengyang Yuan Jian treated him with deep courtesy and each month often ordered his carriage to call at his gate; they talked all day.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator Prince of Hengyang Yuan Jian treated him with deep courtesy and often called at his gate; they talked all day.

sentences.zh: 胤以若邪處勢迫隘，不容學徒，乃遷秦望山。

translations.literal: Yin, because Ruoye's terrain was cramped and could not accommodate disciples, moved to Mount Qinwang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ruoye was cramped for disciples, he moved to Mount Qinwang.

sentences.zh: 山有飛泉，乃起學舍，即林成援，因岩為堵；

translations.literal: On the mountain was a flying spring; he raised a schoolhouse, following the forest for beams and the cliff for walls;
translations.idiomatic: A flying spring flowed; he raised a schoolhouse, beams from the forest, walls from the cliff;

sentences.zh: 別為小合室，寢處其中，躬自啟閉，僮僕無得至者。

translations.literal: separately he built a small chamber and slept within it, opening and closing it himself—servants could not approach.
translations.idiomatic: he built a small chamber and slept within, opening and closing it himself—servants could not approach.

sentences.zh: 山側營田二頃，講隙從生徒遊之。

translations.literal: On the mountainside he cultivated two qing of fields and in intervals between lectures roamed with disciples.
translations.idiomatic: On the mountainside he cultivated two qing and roamed with disciples between lectures.

sentences.zh: 胤初遷將築室，忽見二人著玄冠，容貌甚偉，問胤曰：「君欲居此邪？

translations.literal: When Yin first moved and was about to build a dwelling, he suddenly saw two men wearing dark caps of imposing appearance who asked Yin, "Do you wish to dwell here?"
translations.idiomatic: When about to build, he saw two men in dark caps who asked, "Do you wish to dwell here?"

sentences.zh: 」乃指一處云：「此中殊吉。

translations.literal: They pointed to a place and said, "This place is especially auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: They pointed to a place: "This place is especially auspicious."

sentences.zh: 」忽不復見。

translations.literal: Suddenly they were no longer visible.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly they vanished.

sentences.zh: 胤依言而卜焉。

translations.literal: Yin followed their words and divined there.
translations.idiomatic: Yin took their counsel and chose that site by divination.

sentences.zh: 尋而山發洪水，樹石皆倒拔，唯胤所居室巋然獨存。

translations.literal: Soon a flood burst from the mountain; trees and stones were uprooted, yet only Yin's dwelling stood firm alone.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a flood burst; trees and stones uprooted, yet only Yin's dwelling stood firm.

sentences.zh: 元簡乃命記室參軍鍾嶸作瑞室頌，刻石以旌之。

translations.literal: Yuan Jian ordered Staff Officer Zhong Rong to compose an "Encomium on the Auspicious Chamber" and carve it in stone to honor it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jian ordered Zhong Rong to compose an "Encomium on the Auspicious Chamber" and carve it in stone.

sentences.zh: 及元簡去郡，入山與胤別。

translations.literal: When Yuan Jian left the commandery he entered the mountain to bid Yin farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Jian left the commandery he entered the mountain to bid farewell.

sentences.zh: 胤送至都賜埭，去郡三里，因曰：「僕自棄人事，交遊路斷，自非降貴山藪，豈容復望城邑。

translations.literal: Yin saw him off to Dusi Embankment, three li from the commandery, and said, "I have cast off human affairs; the road of friendship is cut—unless nobles descend to mountain and marsh, how could I again look upon the city?"
translations.idiomatic: Yin saw him off to Dusi Embankment and said, "I have cast off human affairs—unless nobles descend to mountain and marsh, how could I again look upon the city?"

sentences.zh: 此埭之游，於今絕矣。

translations.literal: "This embankment outing ends here today."
translations.idiomatic: "This embankment outing ends today."

sentences.zh: 」執手涕零。

translations.literal: They clasped hands and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Hand in hand they wept.

sentences.zh: 何氏過江，自晉司空充並葬吳西山。

translations.literal: Since the He clan crossed the river, from Jin Minister of Works Chong onward all were buried on Western Mountain of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Since the He clan crossed the river, from Jin Minister of Works Chong onward all were buried on Wu's Western Mountain.

sentences.zh: 胤家世年皆不永，唯祖尚之至七十二。

translations.literal: Yin's family for generations did not live long; only grandfather Shangzhi reached seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: The He clan rarely lived long; only grandfather Shangzhi reached seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 胤年登祖壽，乃移還吳，作別山詩一首，言甚悽愴。

translations.literal: Yin reached his grandfather's span and moved back to Wu, composing a "Poem on Parting from the Mountain" of extremely mournful words.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching his grandfather's span, he moved back to Wu and composed a mournful "Poem on Parting from the Mountain."

sentences.zh: 至吳，居武丘山西寺講經論，學僧復隨之。

translations.literal: Arriving at Wu, he lived at Western Temple on Mount Wuqiu lecturing on scriptures and doctrine; learning monks again followed him.
translations.idiomatic: At Wu he lived at Western Temple on Mount Wuqiu lecturing; learning monks followed.

sentences.zh: 東境守宰經途者，莫不畢至。

translations.literal: Border officials passing by all came without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials passing by all came.

sentences.zh: 胤常禁殺，有虞人逐鹿，鹿徑來趨胤，伏而不動。

translations.literal: Yin always forbade killing; once a hunter chased a deer and the deer ran straight to Yin and lay still without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Yin forbade killing; once a hunted deer ran to Yin and lay still.

sentences.zh: 又有異鳥如鶴紅色，集講堂，馴狎如家禽。

translations.literal: There was also a strange bird like a crane in red; it gathered at the lecture hall tame as domestic fowl.
translations.idiomatic: A strange red crane-like bird gathered at the lecture hall tame as domestic fowl.

sentences.zh: 初，開善寺藏法師與胤遇于秦望山，後還都，卒於鍾山。

translations.literal: Earlier Master Zang of Kaishan Temple met Yin on Mount Qinwang; later returning to the capital he died on Zhong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Master Zang of Kaishan Temple met Yin on Mount Qinwang; later he died on Zhong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 死日，胤在波若寺見一名僧，授胤香爐奩並函書，云：「貧道發自揚都，呈何居士。

translations.literal: On the day of his death Yin at Boruo Temple saw a monk who gave Yin an incense censer case and letter box, saying, "This poor daoist sets out from Yangdu to present to Master He."
translations.idiomatic: On his death day Yin at Boruo Temple saw a monk who gave him a censer case and letter box from Yangdu.

sentences.zh: 」言訖失所在。

translations.literal: When the words ended he vanished.
translations.idiomatic: With that he vanished.

sentences.zh: 胤開函，乃是大莊嚴論，世中未有。

translations.literal: Yin opened the box—it was the Great Treatise on the Adorned, not yet in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yin opened the box—the Great Treatise on the Adorned, not yet in the world.

sentences.zh: 訪之香爐，乃藏公所常用。

translations.literal: Inquiring about the censer, it was what Master Zang commonly used.
translations.idiomatic: The censer was what Master Zang commonly used.

sentences.zh: 又于寺內立明珠柱，柱乃七日七夜放光。

translations.literal: Also within the temple a pearl pillar was erected; for seven days and seven nights it emitted light.
