translations.idiomatic: A pearl pillar was erected; for seven days and seven nights it emitted light.

sentences.zh: 太守何遠以狀啟昭明太子，太子欽其德，遣舍人何思澄致手令以褒美之。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator He Yuan memorialized Crown Prince Zhaoming, who admired his virtue and sent Attendant He Sicheng with a personal order of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator He Yuan memorialized Crown Prince Zhaoming, who sent He Sicheng with praise.

sentences.zh: 中大通三年卒，年八十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong he died at eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong 3 he died at eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 先是胤疾，妻江氏夢神告曰：「汝夫壽盡，既有至德，應獲延期，爾當代之。

translations.literal: Earlier when Yin was ill his wife Lady Jiang dreamed a spirit told her, "Your husband's lifespan is exhausted; because he has supreme virtue he should receive extension—you will replace him."
translations.idiomatic: When Yin was ill Lady Jiang dreamed a spirit said, "Your husband's lifespan is exhausted; for supreme virtue you will replace him."

sentences.zh: 」妻覺說焉，俄得患而卒，胤疾乃瘳。

translations.literal: When his wife awoke and told this, she soon fell ill and died, and Yin's illness then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: She told this, soon fell ill and died, and Yin recovered.

sentences.zh: 至是胤夢見一神女並八十許人，並衣帢，行列在前，俱拜床下，覺又見之，便命營凶具。

translations.literal: Now Yin dreamed he saw a spirit woman and about eighty people all wearing kerchiefs, ranked in rows before him, all bowing below the bed; waking he saw them again and ordered funeral goods prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yin dreamed a spirit woman and eighty kerchiefed people bowing below his bed; waking he ordered funeral goods prepared.

sentences.zh: 既而疾困不復瘳。

translations.literal: Soon his illness worsened and did not recover.
translations.idiomatic: His illness soon deepened and he did not recover.

sentences.zh: 初，胤侈於味，食必方丈，後稍欲去其甚者，猶食白魚、夔脯，糖蟹，以為非見生物。

translations.literal: Earlier Yin was extravagant in taste and each meal required a full table; later he wished to remove the worst yet still ate white fish, pickled mallow, and sugared crab, considering them not seeing living creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier extravagant in taste, each meal a full table; later he still ate white fish, pickled mallow, and sugared crab, considering them not living creatures.

sentences.zh: 疑食蚶蠣，使門人議之。

translations.literal: Doubting oysters and mussels, he had disciples deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Unsure about oysters and mussels, he asked disciples to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 學生鍾岏曰：「夔之就脯，驟于屈申，蟹之將糖，躁擾彌甚。

translations.literal: Disciple Zhong Wan said, "When mallow becomes pickle it suffers more than bending and stretching; when crab receives sugar its agitation is even greater."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Wan said, "Mallow becoming pickle suffers more than bending; crab receiving sugar agitates even more."

sentences.zh: 仁人用意，深懷如怛。

translations.literal: "The humane man's intent—deep feeling like distress."
translations.idiomatic: "In the humane heart, pity runs as deep as pain."

sentences.zh: 至於車螯蚶蠣，眉目內闕，慚渾沌之奇，獷殼外緘，非金人之慎。

translations.literal: "As for cart clams and oysters, eyes and brows are inwardly absent—ashamed before Chaos's marvel; rough shells outwardly sealed—not the Golden Man's caution."
translations.idiomatic: "Cart clams and oysters lack eyes and brows—ashamed before Chaos; rough shells sealed—not the Golden Man's caution."

sentences.zh: 不悴不榮，曾草木之不若，無馨無臭，與瓦礫其何算。

translations.literal: "Neither withered nor flourishing—they do not equal grass and trees; without fragrance or stench—they differ from rubble how?"
translations.idiomatic: "Neither withered nor flourishing—less than grass; without fragrance or stench—how differ from rubble?"

sentences.zh: 故宜長充庖廚，永為口實。

translations.literal: "Therefore they should long fill the kitchen and forever serve the mouth."
translations.idiomatic: "Therefore they should long fill the kitchen and serve the mouth."

sentences.zh: 」竟陵王子良見岏議大怒。

translations.literal: Prince of Jingling Ziliang saw Wan's argument and was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jingling saw Wan's argument and was greatly angered.

sentences.zh: 汝南周顒與胤書，勸令食菜，曰：「變之大者，莫過死生，生之所重，無逾性命。

translations.literal: Zhou Yong of Runan wrote Yin urging him to eat vegetables, saying, "Among great changes none surpass birth and death; among what life values nothing exceeds life itself."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yong urged vegetables: "Among changes none surpass birth and death; among life's values nothing exceeds life."

sentences.zh: 性命之於彼極切，滋味之在我可賒。

translations.literal: "Life to them is most urgent; flavor to us can be deferred."
translations.idiomatic: "Life to them is urgent; flavor to us can be deferred."

sentences.zh: 若雲三世理誣，則幸矣良快，如使此道果然，而受形未息，一往一來，生死常事，則傷心之慘，行亦自及。

translations.literal: "If one says the doctrine of three lives is false, then fortunate and glad; yet if this way is true and form has not ceased, coming and going, birth and death an ordinary affair—then the anguish of wounded heart, in action will also reach you."
translations.idiomatic: "If three lives is false, fortunate; yet if true and form has not ceased, coming and going—then wounded-heart anguish will reach you in action."

sentences.zh: 丈人于血氣之類，雖不身踐，至於晨鳧夜鯉，不能不取備屠門。

translations.literal: "Though you, elder, do not personally tread among blood and flesh, as for morning duck and evening carp, you cannot but draw from the butcher's gate."
translations.idiomatic: "Though you do not tread among blood and flesh, morning duck and evening carp—you cannot but draw from the butcher's gate."

sentences.zh: 財貝之經盜手，猶為廉士所棄，生性之一啟鑾刀，寧復慈心所忍。

translations.literal: "Wealth and goods touched by a thief's hand are still abandoned by the upright man; life opened by the butcher's knife—how can compassionate heart bear it?"
translations.idiomatic: "Wealth touched by a thief's hand the upright abandon; life opened by the butcher's knife—how can compassionate heart bear it?"

sentences.zh: 騶虞雖饑，非自死之草不食，聞其風者，豈不使人多媿。

translations.literal: "Though the Zou-yu starves, it will not eat grass that did not die of itself—those who hear its wind, will they not feel much shame?"
translations.idiomatic: "Though the Zou-yu starves, it will not eat grass that did not die of itself—will hearers not feel shame?"

sentences.zh: 丈人得此有素，聊復片言發起耳。

translations.literal: "You, elder, have long held this— I offer these few words merely to stir you."
translations.idiomatic: "You have long held this—I offer these words merely to stir you."

sentences.zh: 」故胤末年遂絕血味。

translations.literal: Therefore in his later years Yin entirely renounced the taste of blood.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in later years Yin entirely renounced the taste of blood.

sentences.zh: 胤注百論、十二門論各一卷，注周易十卷，毛詩總集六卷，毛詩隱義十卷，禮記隱義二十卷，禮答問五十五卷。

translations.literal: Yin annotated one volume each of the Hundred Treatises and Twelve Gates Treatise, annotated ten volumes of the Book of Changes, six volumes of Collected Commentary on the Mao Odes, ten volumes of Hidden Meaning of the Mao Odes, twenty volumes of Hidden Meaning of the Record of Rites, and fifty-five volumes of Ritual Questions and Answers.
translations.idiomatic: Yin annotated the Hundred Treatises, Twelve Gates, Book of Changes, Mao Odes, Record of Rites, and Ritual Questions and Answers.

sentences.zh: 子撰亦不仕，有高風。

translations.literal: His son Zhuan also did not serve and had lofty character.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhuan also refused office and kept lofty character.

sentences.zh: 何炯字士光，胤從弟也。

translations.literal: He Jiong, styled Shiguang, was Yin's younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: He Jiong, styled Shiguang, was Yin's cousin.

sentences.zh: 父撙，太中大夫。

translations.literal: His father Zun was Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zun held the post of Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 炯年十五，從胤受業，一期並通五經章句。

translations.literal: At fifteen Jiong studied under Yin and in one term mastered the chapter-and-sentence exegesis of all Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Jiong studied under Yin and in one term mastered all Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 白皙美容貌，從兄求、點每曰：「叔寶神清，杜乂膚清，今觀此子，復見衛、杜在目。

translations.literal: Fair-skinned with handsome features, elder cousins Qiu and Dian each said, "Shu-bao's spirit was clear, Du Yi's skin was clear—viewing this child, I again see Wei and Du before my eyes."
translations.idiomatic: Fair and handsome, Qiu and Dian said, "Shu-bao's spirit, Du Yi's skin—viewing this child I again see Wei and Du before my eyes."

sentences.zh: 」從兄戢謂人曰：「此子非止吾門之寶，亦為一代偉人。」

translations.literal: Cousin Ji told someone, "This child is not only our clan's treasure but a great man of the age."
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Ji said, "This child is not only our clan's treasure but a great man of the age."

sentences.zh: 炯常慕恬退，不樂進仕。

translations.literal: Jiong always admired quiet withdrawal and did not delight in advancing to office.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong admired quiet withdrawal and did not delight in office.

sentences.zh: 從叔昌宇謂曰：「求、點皆已高蹈，汝無宜復爾。

translations.literal: Cousin Changyu told him, "Qiu and Dian have both already ascended high— you should not again be like them."
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Changyu said, "Qiu and Dian have ascended high—you should not again be like them."

sentences.zh: 且君子出處亦各一途。」

translations.literal: "Moreover the gentleman's going out and staying each has its path."
translations.idiomatic: "Besides, for a gentleman withdrawal and service are different paths."

sentences.zh: 年十九，解褐揚州主簿，舉秀才，累遷梁仁威南康王限內記室，書侍御史。

translations.literal: At nineteen he began service as Chief Clerk of Yangzhou, was recommended as Outstanding Talent, and was promoted to Recorder within the staff of Prince Renwei of Nankang and Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he became Yangzhou chief clerk, was recommended as Outstanding Talent, and rose to recorder and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 以父疾陳解。

translations.literal: Because of his father's illness he requested release.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill he asked to be released from office.

sentences.zh: 炯侍疾踰旬，衣不解帶，頭不櫛沐，信宿之間，形貌頓改。

translations.literal: Jiong attended the illness for more than ten days without removing his belt or combing his hair; within one or two nights his appearance suddenly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong attended more than ten days without removing belt or combing hair; within nights his appearance changed.

sentences.zh: 及父卒，號慟不絕聲，藉地腰腳虛腫。

translations.literal: When his father died he wailed without ceasing; prostrate on the ground his waist and legs swelled.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he wailed without ceasing; prostrate, waist and legs swelled.

sentences.zh: 醫云：「須服豬蹄湯。

translations.literal: The physician said, "He must take pig-hoof broth."
translations.idiomatic: The doctor said, "He needs pig-hoof broth."

sentences.zh: 」炯以有肉味不肯服，親友請譬，終於不回，遂以毀卒。

translations.literal: Jiong, because it had the taste of meat, would not take it; kin and friends pleaded by analogy, yet in the end he would not turn back and died from grief.
translations.idiomatic: Because it had meat taste he would not take it; kin pleaded, yet he would not turn back and died from grief.

sentences.zh: 先是謂家人曰：「王孫、玄晏所尚不同，長魚、慶緒於事為得。

translations.literal: Earlier he told his family, "Wang-sun and Xuan-yan held different preferences; Chang-yu and Qing-xu got matters right."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he told family, "Wang-sun and Xuan-yan differed; Chang-yu and Qing-xu got matters right."

sentences.zh: 必須儉而中禮，無取苟異。

translations.literal: "One must be frugal yet within ritual—do not seek odd difference."
translations.idiomatic: "Be frugal yet within ritual—do not seek odd difference."

sentences.zh: 月朝十五日，可置一甌粗粥，如常日所進。

translations.literal: "On the first and fifteenth of each month set out one bowl of coarse porridge as on ordinary days."
translations.idiomatic: "On the first and fifteenth set out one bowl of coarse porridge as on ordinary days."

sentences.zh: 」又傷兩兄並淡仕進，故祿所不及，恐而今而後，溫飽無資。

translations.literal: Also grieving that both elder brothers lightly sought office and salary did not reach them, he feared that hereafter warmth and fullness would have no support.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving that elder brothers lightly sought office and salary did not reach them, he feared warmth and fullness would have no support.

sentences.zh: 乃漼然下泣，自外無所言。

translations.literal: He wept profusely and beyond that said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He wept profusely and said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 何昌宇字儼望，尚之弟子也。

translations.literal: He Changyu, styled Yanwang, was Shangzhi's younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: He Changyu, styled Yanwang, was Shangzhi's nephew.

sentences.zh: 父佟之，位侍中。

translations.literal: His father Tongzhi served as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tongzhi had been Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 昌宇少而清靖，獨立不群，所交者必當世清名，是以風流籍甚。

translations.literal: Changyu from youth was pure and tranquil, standing alone apart from the crowd; those he befriended were always men of clear name of the age—therefore his elegant reputation was greatly established.
translations.idiomatic: From youth pure and tranquil, apart from the crowd, he befriended men of clear name—his elegant reputation was greatly established.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為尚書儀曹郎、建平王景素征北南徐州府主簿，以風素見重。

translations.literal: Serving Song he was Director in the Ministry of Rites for Ceremonies and Staff Officer on Prince Jing of Ping's northern campaign staff for Southern Xuzhou; he was valued for his pure character.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Song he was rites director and staff officer on Prince Jing of Ping's campaign staff; valued for pure character.

sentences.zh: 母老求祿，出為湘東太守。

translations.literal: When his mother grew old he sought salary and went out as Grand Administrator of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His mother aging, he sought a salary and went out as Grand Administrator of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 還為齊高帝驃騎功曹。

translations.literal: Returning he became Staff Officer on Qi Emperor Gao's Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Returning he became staff officer on Emperor Gao's Rapid Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 昌宇在郡，景素被誅，昌宇痛之，至是啟高帝理其冤，又與司空褚彥回書極言之。

translations.literal: While Changyu was in the commandery Prince Jingsu was executed; Changyu grieved deeply and now memorialized Emperor Gao to rectify the injustice, also writing Minister of Works Chu Yanhui at length.
translations.idiomatic: While in commandery Prince Jingsu was executed; Changyu memorialized to rectify the injustice and wrote Chu Yanhui at length.

sentences.zh: 高帝嘉其義。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao commended his integrity.

sentences.zh: 歷位中書郎、王儉衛軍長史，儉謂昌宇曰：「後任朝事者，非卿而誰？」

translations.literal: He successively served as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat and Senior Administrator on Wang Jian's Guard Army staff; Jian told Changyu, "Who but you will later handle court affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: He served as Secretariat attendant and Wang Jian's senior administrator; Jian said, "Who but you will handle court affairs?"

sentences.zh: 臨海王昭秀為荊州，以昌宇為西中郎長史、南郡太守，行荊州事。

translations.literal: Prince Zhaoxiu of Linhai was in Jing Province; Changyu was Senior Administrator on the Western General's staff and Grand Administrator of Nan Commandery, acting for Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhaoxiu of Linhai was in Jing; Changyu was senior administrator and Grand Administrator of Nan, acting for Jing.

sentences.zh: 明帝將踐阼，先使裴叔業喪旨詔昌宇，令以便宜從事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was about to ascend the throne he first sent Pei Shuye with mourning edict to Changyu, ordering him to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming was about to ascend he sent Pei Shuye with mourning edict, ordering action as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 昌宇拒之曰：「國家委身以上流之重，付身以萬里之事，臨海王未有失，寧得從君單詔邪？

translations.literal: Changyu refused and said, "The state entrusted me with the weight of the upper stream and entrusted me with affairs ten thousand li away; Prince Linhai has no fault—how can I follow your solitary edict?"
translations.idiomatic: Changyu refused: "The state entrusted me with the upper stream; Prince Linhai has no fault—how follow your solitary edict?"

sentences.zh: 即時自有啟聞，須反更議。

translations.literal: "I will immediately submit a memorial myself; we must return and deliberate again."
translations.idiomatic: "I will submit a memorial; we must return and deliberate."

sentences.zh: 」叔業曰：「若爾便是拒詔，拒詔，軍法行事耳。

translations.literal: Shuye said, "If so this is refusing the edict; refusing the edict—military law will act."
translations.idiomatic: Shuye said, "Then this is refusing the edict—military law will act."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「能見殺者君也，能拒詔者僕也。

translations.literal: He answered, "He who can kill me is the lord; he who can refuse the edict is I."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Only the lord can kill me; only I can refuse the edict."

sentences.zh: 君不能見殺，政有沿流之計耳。

translations.literal: "The lord cannot kill me—there is only the plan of going downstream."
translations.idiomatic: "The lord cannot kill me—there is only going downstream."

sentences.zh: 」昌宇素有名德，叔業不敢逼而退。

translations.literal: Changyu had long had fame and virtue; Shuye did not dare press and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Changyu had fame and virtue; Shuye did not dare press and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之，昭秀由此得還都。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and praised him; Zhaoxiu thereby returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heard and praised him; Zhaoxiu returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 昌宇後為吏部尚書，嘗有一客姓閔求官。

translations.literal: Later Changyu became Director of the Ministry of Personnel; once a guest surnamed Min sought office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became personnel director; once a guest surnamed Min sought office.

sentences.zh: 昌宇謂曰：「君是誰後？

translations.literal: Changyu asked, "Whose descendant are you?"
translations.idiomatic: Changyu asked, "Whose line do you claim?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「子騫後。

translations.literal: He answered, "Descendant of Ziqian."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "A descendant of Min Ziqian."

sentences.zh: 」昌宇團扇掩口而笑，謂坐客曰：「遙遙華胄。」

translations.literal: Changyu covered his mouth with a round fan and laughed, telling those seated, "A distant noble lineage."
translations.idiomatic: Changyu covered his mouth with a round fan and laughed: "A distant noble lineage."

sentences.zh: 昌宇不雜交遊，通和泛愛，曆郡皆以清白稱。

translations.literal: Changyu did not mix in social intercourse yet was universally harmonious and loving; in successive commanderies he was all called pure and white.
translations.idiomatic: He did not mix in social intercourse yet was universally harmonious; in commanderies he was called pure and white.

sentences.zh: 後卒於侍中，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Later he died as Palace Attendant and General of the Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Palace Attendant and General of the Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 贈太常，諡曰簡子。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Grand Master of Ceremonies with the posthumous title Duke of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Grand Master of Ceremonies with title Duke of Jian.

sentences.zh: 子敬容。

translations.literal: His son Jingrong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingrong.

sentences.zh: 敬容字國禮，弱冠尚齊武帝女長城公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Jingrong, styled Guoli, at twenty was matched to Emperor Wu of Qi's daughter Princess of Changcheng and was appointed Commandant of the Horse for the Emperor's Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong, styled Guoli, at twenty married Princess of Changcheng and became Commandant of the Horse.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，為建安內史，清公有美績，吏人稱之。

translations.literal: In Liang Tianjian he was Interior Minister of Jian'an; pure and public with fine achievements, officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian he was Interior Minister of Jian'an; pure and public with fine achievements.

sentences.zh: 累遷守吏部尚書，銓序明審，號為稱職。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel; his ordering was clear and careful and he was called competent.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to personnel director; ordering clear and careful, called competent.

sentences.zh: 出為吳郡太守，為政勤恤人隱，辯訟如神，視事四年，政為天下第一。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Wu Commandery; diligent in governance and caring for people's hidden woes, judging lawsuits like a spirit— in four years his governance was first under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Wu; judging lawsuits like a spirit—in four years governance first under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 吏人詣闕請樹碑，詔許之。

translations.literal: Officials and people went to court requesting a stele; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people requested a stele; an edict permitted.

sentences.zh: 復為吏部尚書、侍中，領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He again became Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Palace Attendant, concurrently Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Again personnel director, Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 敬容身長八尺，白皙美鬚眉，性矜莊，衣冠鮮麗。

translations.literal: Jingrong was eight chi tall, fair-skinned with handsome beard and brows; by nature proud and solemn, his cap and robes were bright and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: Eight chi tall, fair with handsome beard and brows, proud and solemn, cap and robes bright.

sentences.zh: 武帝雖衣浣衣，而左右衣必須潔。

translations.literal: Though Emperor Wu wore washed clothes, those around him had to be clean.
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Wu wore washed clothes, attendants had to be clean.

sentences.zh: 嘗有侍臣衣帶卷折，帝怒曰：「卿衣帶如繩，欲何所縛。

translations.literal: Once a attending minister's belt was creased and folded; the Emperor angrily said, "Your belt is like rope—what do you intend to bind?"
translations.idiomatic: Once a minister's belt was creased; the Emperor said, "Your belt is like rope—what do you intend to bind?"

sentences.zh: 」敬容希旨，故益鮮明。

translations.literal: Jingrong pleased the intent and therefore grew ever more bright.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong pleased the intent and grew ever more bright.

sentences.zh: 常以膠清刷須，衣裳不整，伏床熨之，或暑月背為之焦。

translations.literal: He often brushed his beard with clear glue; if robes were not neat he lay prostrate on the bed to iron them, and in summer months his back was scorched for it.
translations.idiomatic: He brushed his beard with clear glue; if robes were not neat he ironed them prostrate—summer months scorched his back.

sentences.zh: 每公庭就列，容止出人。

translations.literal: Each time he took his place in the public court his bearing surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Each court session his bearing surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 為尚書右僕射，參掌選事。

translations.literal: As Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat he shared charge of selection.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Vice Director he shared charge of selection.

sentences.zh: 遷左僕射、丹陽尹，並參掌大選如故。

translations.literal: Promoted to Left Vice Director and Governor of Danyang, still sharing great selection as before.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted Left Vice Director and Governor of Danyang, still sharing great selection.

sentences.zh: 敬容接對賓朋，言詞若訥，酬答二宮，則音韻調暢。

translations.literal: Jingrong received guests with words seemingly slow, yet answering the two palaces his tone was harmonious and fluent.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving guests his words seemed slow; answering the two palaces his tone was fluent.

sentences.zh: 大同中，朱雀門災，武帝謂群臣曰：「此門制狹，我始欲改構，遂遭天火。

translations.literal: In Datong the Vermilion Bird Gate caught fire; Emperor Wu told the ministers, "This gate's design is narrow—I originally wished to rebuild it and then met heaven's fire."
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion Bird Gate caught fire; Emperor Wu said, "This gate is narrow—I wished to rebuild and met heaven's fire."

sentences.zh: 」相顧未答，敬容獨曰：「此所謂先天而天不違。

translations.literal: They looked at one another without answer; Jingrong alone said, "This is what is called anticipating Heaven so Heaven does not oppose."
translations.idiomatic: None answered; Jingrong alone said, "This is anticipating Heaven so Heaven does not oppose."

sentences.zh: 」時以為名對。

translations.literal: People of the time considered it a famous reply.
translations.idiomatic: People considered it a famous reply.

sentences.zh: 五年，改為尚書令，參選事如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Director of the Imperial Secretariat, charge of selection unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat, selection unchanged.

sentences.zh: 敬容久處台閣，詳悉晉魏以來舊事，且聰明識達，勤於簿領，詰朝理事，日旰不休。

translations.literal: Jingrong long dwelt in the secretariat, thoroughly knowing affairs from Jin and Wei onward; moreover clever and penetrating, diligent in ledgers—he handled court business from dawn until sunset without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Long in the secretariat, knowing affairs from Jin and Wei; clever, diligent in ledgers—handling business from dawn to sunset.

sentences.zh: 職隆任重，專預機密，而拙於草隸，淺於學術，通包苴餉饋，無賄則略不交語。

translations.literal: Office was lofty and burden heavy; he alone shared in secrets, yet clumsy at draft script and shallow in learning, universally accepting bribes and gifts—without bribes he barely exchanged words.
translations.idiomatic: Office lofty, sharing secrets, yet clumsy at script and shallow in learning—without bribes he barely spoke.

sentences.zh: 自晉宋以來，宰相皆文義自逸，敬容獨勤庶務，貪吝為時所嗤鄙。

translations.literal: Since Jin and Song, chancellors all rested in literary elegance; Jingrong alone toiled in common affairs and was scorned for greed.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin and Song chancellors rested in literary elegance; Jingrong toiled in affairs and was scorned for greed.

sentences.zh: 其署名「敬」字，則大作「苟」，小為「文」，「容」字大為「父」，小為「口」。

translations.literal: When he signed his name the character "Jing" he wrote large as "Gou" and small as "Wen"; the character "Rong" he wrote large as "Fu" and small as "Kou."
translations.idiomatic: Signing his name "Jing" he wrote large as "Gou" small as "Wen"; "Rong" large as "Fu" small as "Kou."

sentences.zh: 陸倕戲之曰：「公家'苟'既奇大，'父'亦不小。

translations.literal: Lu Chuo jested, "Your family's 'Gou' is already strangely large and 'Fu' is not small either."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chuo jested, "Your 'Gou' is strangely large and 'Fu' not small either."

sentences.zh: 」敬容遂不能答。

translations.literal: Jingrong then could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong could not answer.

sentences.zh: 又多漏禁中語，故嘲誚日至。

translations.literal: He also often leaked words from within the forbidden palace; therefore mockery arrived daily.
translations.idiomatic: He often leaked forbidden-palace words; mockery arrived daily.

sentences.zh: 嘗有客姓吉，敬容問：「卿與邴吉遠近？

translations.literal: Once a guest surnamed Ji; Jingrong asked, "How far are you from Bing Ji?"
translations.idiomatic: Once a guest surnamed Ji; Jingrong asked, "How far from Bing Ji?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「如明公之與蕭何。

translations.literal: He answered, "Like your Excellency from Xiao He."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "About as close as your Excellency is to Xiao He."

sentences.zh: 」時蕭琛子巡頗有輕薄才，因制卦名、離合等詩嘲之，亦不屑也。

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Chen's son Xun had rather frivolous talent and composed hexagram names, separation-combination poems, and the like to mock him; Jingrong also paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chen's son Xun composed hexagram and separation-combination poems to mock him; Jingrong paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗夢具朝服入太廟拜伏悲感，旦於延務殿說所夢。

translations.literal: The Emperor once dreamed he wore full court robes, entered the Imperial Ancestral Temple, bowed prostrate and was moved to grief; at dawn in Yanswu Hall he told the dream.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dreamed full court robes in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, bowing moved to grief; at dawn he told the dream.

sentences.zh: 敬容對曰：「臣聞孝悌之至，通於神明。

translations.literal: Jingrong replied, "I hear that filial piety and brotherly respect at their utmost penetrate to the spirits."
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong replied, "Filial piety at utmost penetrates to the spirits."

sentences.zh: 陛下性與天通，故應感斯夢。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty's nature accords with Heaven—therefore you were moved by this dream."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty's nature accords with Heaven—therefore this dream."

sentences.zh: 」上極然之，便有拜陵之議。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly agreed and thereupon arose the plan to visit the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor greatly agreed and arose the plan to visit tombs.

sentences.zh: 後坐妾弟費慧明為道倉丞夜盜官米，為禁司所執，送領軍府。

translations.literal: Later because his concubine's younger brother Fei Huiming as Director of the Way Granary stole official grain at night and was seized by the prohibition office, he was sent to the Army Commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: Later concubine's brother Fei Huiming stole official grain and was sent to the Army Commander's office.

sentences.zh: 時河東王譽為領軍，敬容以書解慧明。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Hedong Yu was Army Commander; Jingrong wrote a letter exonerating Huiming.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hedong Yu was Army Commander; Jingrong wrote exonerating Huiming.

sentences.zh: 譽前經屬事不行，因此即封書以奏。

translations.literal: Yu had earlier requested a matter that was not granted; therefore he sealed the letter and memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had earlier requested a matter not granted; he sealed the letter and memorialized.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，付南司推劾。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and handed it to the southern bureau for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged and handed it to the southern bureau.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞張綰奏敬容協私罔上，合棄市。

translations.literal: Imperial Censor Zhang Chuo memorialized that Jingrong favored private interest and deceived superiors—punishment fitting abandonment at the market.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chuo memorialized favoring private interest and deceiving superiors—punishment fitting market abandonment.

sentences.zh: 詔特免職。

translations.literal: An edict specially removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped him of office by special grace.

sentences.zh: 到溉謂朱異曰：「天時便覺開霽。

translations.literal: Dao Gai told Zhu Yi, "The weather now feels clearing after rain."
translations.idiomatic: Dao Gai told Zhu Yi, "The sky feels as if rain has just cleared."

sentences.zh: 」其見嫉如此。

translations.literal: Such was the envy he aroused.
translations.idiomatic: So bitter was the envy against him.

sentences.zh: 初，沙門釋寶志嘗謂敬容曰：「君後必貴，終是'何'敗耳。

translations.literal: Earlier the monk Shizhi once told Jingrong, "You will later surely be noble— in the end it is 'He' that ruins you."
translations.idiomatic: Monk Shizhi told Jingrong, "You will be noble—in the end 'He' ruins you."

sentences.zh: 」及敬容為宰相，謂何姓當為其禍，故抑沒宗族，無仕進者，至是竟為河東所敗。

translations.literal: When Jingrong became chancellor he thought the He surname would be his calamity and therefore suppressed his clan with none advancing to office; yet in the end he was ruined by Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor he thought He would be his calamity and suppressed his clan; yet Hedong ruined him.

sentences.zh: 中大同元年三月，武帝幸同泰寺講金字三慧經，敬容啟預聽，敕許之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Zhongdatong Emperor Wu visited Tongtai Temple to lecture on the Golden-character Three Wisdom Sutra; Jingrong memorialized to attend listening and an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongdatong year 1 month 3 Emperor Wu visited Tongtai Temple; Jingrong memorialized to attend and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 又起為金紫光祿大夫，未拜，又加侍中。

translations.literal: He was again raised as Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; before accepting he was again added as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Raised Grand Master with golden seal; before accepting, added Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 敬容舊時賓客門生喧嘩如昔，冀其復用。

translations.literal: Jingrong's old guests and disciples clamored as before, hoping for his reuse.
translations.idiomatic: Old guests and disciples clamored as before, hoping for reuse.

sentences.zh: 會稽謝鬱致書戒之曰：

translations.literal: Kuaiji Xie Yu wrote a letter admonishing him:
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji Xie Yu wrote admonishing:

sentences.zh: 草萊之人，聞諸道路，君侯已得瞻望朝夕，出入禁門。

translations.literal: A man of grass and wilds, hearing on the road, has learned that my lord already obtains morning and evening audience and goes in and out of the forbidden gate.
translations.idiomatic: A man of grass and wilds, hearing on the road, learns my lord already obtains audience and goes in and out of the forbidden gate.

sentences.zh: 醉尉將不敢呵，灰然不無其漸，甚休！

translations.literal: The drunken gatekeeper will not dare shout; gradually there is no lack of progress— excellent!
translations.idiomatic: The drunken gatekeeper will not dare shout; gradually there is progress—excellent!

sentences.zh: 敢賀於前，又將吊也。

translations.literal: I dare congratulate you beforehand, yet will also condole.
translations.idiomatic: I dare congratulate beforehand, yet will also condole.

sentences.zh: 昔流言裁至，公旦東奔，燕書始來，子孟不入。

translations.literal: In former times when slander just arrived, Duke of Zhou fled east; when the letter from Yan first came, Huo Guang did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: When slander arrived Duke of Zhou fled east; when Yan's letter came Huo Guang did not enter.

sentences.zh: 夫聖賢被虛過以自斥，未有嬰時釁而求親者也。

translations.literal: Sages and worthies use empty faults to reproach themselves— never has one sought intimacy at a moment of taint.
translations.idiomatic: Sages use empty faults to reproach themselves—never seek intimacy at a moment of taint.

sentences.zh: 且暴鰓之魚，不念杯酌之水，雲霄之翼，豈顧籠樊之糧。

translations.literal: Moreover a fish with bursting gills does not think of cup and ladle water; wings in the clouds— how would they look to cage and railing feed?
translations.idiomatic: A fish with bursting gills does not think of cup water; cloud wings—how look to cage feed?

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 所托已盛也。

translations.literal: What they rely on is already grand.
translations.idiomatic: What they lean on is already exalted.

sentences.zh: 昔君侯納言加首，鳴玉在腰，回豐貂以步文昌，聳高蟬而趨武帳，可謂盛矣。

translations.literal: In former days my lord received the word "Counselor" added to your head and jade pendants at your waist; turning the rich sable you walked through Wenchang, raising the high cicada you hastened to the martial tent— it could be called flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly you received "Counselor" at head and jade at waist; rich sable through Wenchang, high cicada to the martial tent—flourishing.

sentences.zh: 不以此時薦才拔士，少報聖主之恩，今卒如爰絲之說，受責見過，方復欲更窺朝廷，觖望萬分，竊不為左右取也。

translations.literal: Not then recommending talent and raising scholars to repay the sage lord's grace— now suddenly like Ai Si's saying, receiving blame and visible fault, yet again wishing to peep at court and hope for ten thousand parts— I secretly do not take this for your side.
translations.idiomatic: Not then recommending talent to repay grace—now like Ai Si's saying, receiving blame, yet again peeping at court—I do not take this for your side.

sentences.zh: 昔竇嬰、楊惲亦得罪明時，不能謝絕賓客，猶交黨援，卒無後福，終益前禍。

translations.literal: In former times Dou Ying and Yang Yun also offended their enlightened age yet could not break with guests and still exchanged faction support— in the end no later blessing, finally adding to former calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying and Yang Yun offended their age yet could not break with guests—no later blessing, adding to calamity.

sentences.zh: 僕之所吊，實在於斯。

translations.literal: What I condole for is truly here.
translations.idiomatic: That is what I mourn for you.

sentences.zh: 人人所以頗猶有踵君侯之門者，未必皆感惠懷仁，有灌夫、任安之義，乃戒翟公之大署，冀君侯之復用也。

translations.literal: Why people still somewhat follow my lord's gate— not necessarily all moved by kindness and benevolence with Guan Fu and Ren An's righteousness, but warning against Duke Zhai's great inscription, hoping for my lord's reuse.
translations.idiomatic: Why people still follow your gate—not all moved by Ren An's righteousness, but warning against Duke Zhai's inscription, hoping for reuse.

sentences.zh: 夫在思過之日，而挾復用之意，未可為智者說矣。

translations.literal: On days of reflecting on faults, yet carrying intent of reuse— this cannot be told to the wise.
translations.idiomatic: On days of reflecting on faults, yet carrying reuse intent—this cannot be told to the wise.

sentences.zh: 夫君侯宜杜門念失，無有所通，築茅茨於鍾阜，聊優遊以卒歲，見可憐之意，著待終之情，復仲尼能改之言，惟子貢更也之譬，少戢言於眾口，微自救於竹帛，所謂「失之東隅，收之桑榆」。

translations.literal: My lord should shut the gate and reflect on loss without communicating; build a thatched hut on Zhong Mountain and leisurely roam to end your years— show pitiable intent, display awaiting-end feeling, restore Confucius's words on reform, recall Zigong's "change it" analogy, slightly restrain words from many mouths, subtly save yourself in written records— this is "losing the eastern corner, gaining the mulberry dusk."
translations.idiomatic: Shut the gate and reflect; build a hut on Zhong Mountain—show pitiable intent, restore reform, restrain many mouths—"losing the eastern corner, gaining mulberry dusk."

sentences.zh: 如此，令明主聞知，尚有冀也。

translations.literal: Thus let the enlightened lord hear and know— there is still hope.
translations.idiomatic: Thus let the enlightened lord hear—there is still hope.

sentences.zh: 僕東皋鄙人，入穴幸無銜寠，恥天下之士，不為執事道之，故披肝膽，示情素，君侯豈能鑒焉。

translations.literal: I am a rustic of the eastern marsh, entering the cave fortunately without bitter taste; ashamed that gentlemen under Heaven would not speak for you— therefore I lay bare liver and gall, show true feeling; can my lord discern it?
translations.idiomatic: I am a rustic of eastern marsh; ashamed gentlemen would not speak for you—I lay bare liver and gall; can you discern?

sentences.zh: 太清元年，遷太子詹事，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing he was transferred Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Palace Attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Taiqing 1 he became Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Palace Attendant unchanged.

sentences.zh: 二年，侯景襲建鄴，敬容自府移家台內。

translations.literal: In the second year Hou Jing raided Jianye; Jingrong moved his household from his office into the platform interior.
translations.idiomatic: Year 2 Hou Jing raided Jianye; Jingrong moved household into the platform interior.

sentences.zh: 初，景渦陽退敗，未得審實，傳者乃雲其將暴顯反，景身與眾並沒。

translations.literal: Earlier when Jing retreated defeated at Woyang the facts were not yet verified; transmitters then said he would suddenly rebel and Jing himself and the multitude were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing retreated at Woyang facts were unverified; transmitters said he would rebel and all were lost.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以為憂。

translations.literal: The court considered it worry.
translations.idiomatic: The court was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 敬容尋見東宮，簡文謂曰：「淮北始更有信，侯景定得身免。

translations.literal: Jingrong soon saw the Eastern Palace; Emperor Jianwen said, "North of the Huai there is finally more news— Hou Jing will surely escape with his life."
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong saw the Eastern Palace; Emperor Jianwen said, "North of the Huai there is news—Hou Jing will escape."

sentences.zh: 」敬容曰：「得景遂死，深是朝廷之福。

translations.literal: Jingrong said, "If Jing then dies, deeply the court's fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong said, "If Jing is dead, that is the court's great fortune."

sentences.zh: 」簡文失色，問其故，對曰：「景翻覆叛臣，終當亂國。」

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen turned pale and asked the reason; he answered, "Jing is a treacherous rebel minister— in the end he will disorder the state."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen turned pale; he answered, "Jing is a treacherous rebel—in the end he will disorder the state."

sentences.zh: 是年，簡文頻于玄圃自講老莊二書，學士吳孜時寄詹事府，每日入聽。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Jianwen frequently lectured on Laozi and Zhuangzi at the Mysterious Garden himself; scholar Wu Zi then lodged at the Grand Tutor's office and daily entered to listen.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Jianwen lectured on Laozi and Zhuangzi at Mysterious Garden; Wu Zi lodged at the Grand Tutor's office and daily listened.

sentences.zh: 敬容謂孜曰：「昔晉氏喪亂，頗由祖尚虛玄，胡賊遂覆中夏。

translations.literal: Jingrong told Zi, "In the Jin house disorder largely arose from ancestor Shang's empty abstruse talk—the barbarian bandits then overturned central Xia."
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong told Zi, "Jin disorder largely arose from ancestor Shang's empty abstruse talk—barbarians overturned central Xia."

sentences.zh: 今東宮復襲此，殆非人事，其將為戎乎。

translations.literal: "Now the Eastern Palace again follows this— scarcely human affairs; will it not become war?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now the Eastern Palace again follows this—scarcely human affairs; will it not become war?"

sentences.zh: 」俄而侯景難作，其言有征也。

translations.literal: Soon Hou Jing's calamity arose; his words were verified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hou Jing's rebellion broke out, just as he had said.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒於圍內。

translations.literal: In the third year he died within the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Year 3 he died within the siege.

sentences.zh: 何氏自晉司空充、宋司空尚之奉佛法，並建立塔寺，至敬容又舍宅東為伽藍，趨權者因助財造構，敬容並不拒，故寺堂宇頗為宏麗。

translations.literal: The He clan from Jin Minister of Works Chong and Song Minister of Works Shangzhi honored Buddhism, all establishing pagodas and temples; to Jingrong again he donated his eastern residence as a monastery— power-seekers therefore helped with funds to build, and Jingrong refused none; therefore the temple halls were quite grand and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: From Chong and Shangzhi the He clan honored Buddhism; Jingrong donated his eastern residence—power-seekers helped build and he refused none; temple halls were grand.

sentences.zh: 時輕薄者因呼為「眾造寺」。

translations.literal: Frivolous people of the time therefore called it the "Mass-built Temple."
translations.idiomatic: Frivolous people called it the "Mass-built Temple."

sentences.zh: 及敬容免職出宅，止有常用器物及囊衣而已，竟無餘財貨，時亦以此稱之。

translations.literal: When Jingrong was removed from office and left his residence he had only ordinary utensils and bagged clothes— ultimately no surplus wealth; people of the time also praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Removed from office he had only ordinary utensils and bagged clothes—no surplus wealth; people praised this.

sentences.zh: 敬容特為從兄胤所親愛，胤在若邪山嘗疾篤，有書云：「田疇館宇悉奉眾僧，書經並歸從弟敬容。

translations.literal: Jingrong was specially loved by cousin Yin; Yin on Mount Ruoye once was gravely ill and left a letter: "Fields, lodges, and halls all given to the assembly of monks; copied scriptures all go to cousin Jingrong."
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Yin specially loved him; gravely ill on Mount Ruoye Yin left: "Fields and halls to monks; scriptures to cousin Jingrong."

sentences.zh: 」其見知如此。

translations.literal: Such was the regard he received.
translations.idiomatic: So highly was he regarded.

sentences.zh: 敬容唯有一子，年始八歲。

translations.literal: Jingrong had only one son, just eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: He had only one son, just eight years old.

sentences.zh: 在吳，臨還與胤別，胤問名，敬容曰：「仍欲就兄求名。

translations.literal: In Wu, about to return he bade Yin farewell; Yin asked the name; Jingrong said, "I still wish to ask my elder brother for a name."
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, about to return he bade farewell; Yin asked the name; Jingrong said, "I wish to ask elder brother for a name."

sentences.zh: 」胤即命紙筆，名曰玨。

translations.literal: Yin immediately ordered paper and brush and named him Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Yin ordered paper and brush and named him Jue.

sentences.zh: 曰：「書雲兩玉曰玨，吾與弟二家共此一子，所謂鈺也。

translations.literal: He said, "The writing says two jade makes jue— my brother and I two families share this one child, what is called yu."
translations.idiomatic: "Two jade makes jue—two families share this one child, called yu."

sentences.zh: 」位秘書丞，早卒。

translations.literal: He served as Secretary Assistant and died young.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Secretary Assistant and died young.

sentences.zh: 論曰：尚之以雅道自居，用致公輔，行己之跡，動不踰閑。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Shangzhi took elegant conduct as his dwelling and thereby reached chancellor; the traces of his conduct never overstepped propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal: Shangzhi took elegant conduct as dwelling and reached chancellor; conduct never overstepped propriety.

sentences.zh: 及乎洗合取譏，皮冠獲誚，貞粹之地，高人未之全許。

translations.literal: Yet when washing and combining brought ridicule and the deerskin cap earned mockery, in the ground of pure integrity the lofty man did not wholly approve.
translations.idiomatic: Yet washing and combining brought ridicule and deerskin cap mockery—in pure integrity the lofty man did not wholly approve.

sentences.zh: 然父子一時並處權要，雖經屯詖，咸以功名自卒，古之所謂巧宦，此之謂乎。

translations.literal: Yet father and son at one time both held positions of power; though they passed through slander, all ended in merit and name themselves— what antiquity called the clever office-seeker—is this not that?
translations.idiomatic: Yet father and son both held power; though passing slander, all ended in merit—what antiquity called clever office-seeker—is this not that?

sentences.zh: 點、胤弟兄俱雲遁逸，求其蹈履，則非曰山林，察其持身，則未舍名譽。

translations.literal: Dian and Yin brothers both claimed reclusion; seeking their tread, it is not called mountain and forest; examining their self-conduct, they did not leave reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Dian and Yin claimed reclusion; their tread was not mountain and forest; their conduct did not leave reputation.

sentences.zh: 觀夫子皙之赴慧景，子季之矯敬沖，以跡以心，居然可測。

translations.literal: Observing Zixi's going to Huijing and Ziji's correcting respect and restraint— by act and by heart, clearly they could be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi going to Huijing and Ziji correcting restraint—by act and heart, clearly measured.

sentences.zh: 而高自標緻，一代歸宗，以之入用，未知所取。

translations.literal: Yet they highly marked themselves as refined and the age returned to them as masters— to put them to use, one does not know what to take.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they marked themselves refined and the age returned to them— to put them to use, one does not know what to take.

sentences.zh: 斯殆虛勝之風，江東所尚，不然何以至於此也？

translations.literal: This is perhaps the wind of empty victory that Jiangdong honors— otherwise how reach this?
translations.idiomatic: This is perhaps empty-victory wind that Jiangdong honors—otherwise how reach this?

sentences.zh: 昌宇雅仗名節，殆曰人望。

translations.literal: Changyu elegantly relied on fame and integrity— nearly called the people's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Changyu relied on fame and integrity—nearly the people's expectation.

sentences.zh: 敬容材實幹蠱，賄而敗業，惜乎。

translations.literal: Jingrong had talent and substance and handled affairs, yet was ruined by bribes— pity.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong had talent and handled affairs, yet was ruined by bribes—pity.
